items.title: Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS)
items.description: Explore Siemens Energy’s flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) to enhance AC grid reliability, boost power quality, and increase transmission capacity.

faqs.q: Why do we need grid stabilization?
faqs.a: Since power is produced on demand, it's critical to ensure that the power system frequency and voltage remains within nominal ranges. Maintaining this balance is necessary to keep the power grid stable and efficient.

faqs.q: What are flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) and its application?
faqs.a: FACTS are power electronic based devices used to improve the controllability and increase the power transfer capability of AC transmission systems by absorbing and providing of reactive power.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of FACTS?
faqs.a: FACTS can provide high dynamic reactive power to respond to voltage fluctuations caused by load changes or faults in the grid.

faqs.q: What are the main types of FACTS devices?
faqs.a: The main types of flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) devices include STATCOM (SVC PLUS®), E-STATCOM (SVC PLUS® FS), synchronous condenser, fixed series capacitor (FSC), and mechanically switched capacitors (MSC and MSCDN). These devices are integral to enhancing grid stability and efficiency.

faqs.q: How do FACTS support renewable energy integration?
faqs.a: FACTS devices support the integration of renewable energy sources like wind and solar by enhancing grid stability, adaptability, and resilience. They manage the variability and intermittency of renewables by dynamically controlling voltage and reactive power, allowing for efficient power flow management. This ensures seamless integration into the grid, maintaining balance between supply and demand as renewable penetration increases, ultimately contributing to a more reliable and responsive power system.

faqs.q: Can FACTS increase the capacity of existing transmission lines?
faqs.a: Yes, FACTS can significantly increase the capacity of existing transmission lines. FACTS devices enhance grid performance by absorbing or providing reactive power, which improves the power transfer capability and efficiency of AC transmission systems. By optimizing the flow of electricity through the existing infrastructure, FACTS devices enable higher power transfer capabilities, reducing the need for constructing new transmission lines. This optimization allows for more efficient use of current assets, ultimately increasing the overall capacity of the transmission network.

faqs.q: How is Siemens Energy advancing FACTS technology?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy advances FACTS technology by constantly optimizing existing solutions and developing new features. Our commitment to innovation ensures that FACTS devices continue to meet evolving grid demands, enhancing performance and reliability in modern power systems.

faqs.q: Why do grids need power factor correction?
faqs.a: Without power factor correction the power lines and other equipment would be utilized with reactive power which limits utilization with active power and will not operate at optimal condition.

faqs.q: What is grid-forming?
faqs.a: Grid-forming FACTS devices can operate on very weak grids, while grid-following devices require a more stable grid. Grid-forming devices use their built-in active power source to respond inherent to grid events.

faqs.q: Which additional features can be provided by FACTS?
faqs.a: Main additional features are: active harmonic filtering up to four different harmonics simultaneouslyload balancing (negative phase sequence control)POD (power oscillation damping)

Siemens Energy operates globally, bringing extensive expertise in addressing technical and environmental challenges within transmission grids. items.title: Converter Controlled Series Capacitors (CCSC PLUS)
items.description: CCSC PLUS is Siemens Energy’s FACTS-based platform for dynamic power flow control and series compensation in high-voltage grids.

specs.value: Up to 400 kV (higher voltages on request)

specs.name: Additional functions
specs.value: POD, SSR/SSTI mitigation, Emergency dispatch, Line overload management

faqs.q: What are Converter Controlled Series Capacitors (CCSC PLUS)?
faqs.a: CCSC PLUS is Siemens Energy's platform-based dynamic series compensation solution for high-voltage AC transmission grids. It combines a fixed series capacitor with a converter branch based on voltage source converter (VSC) and modular multilevel converter (MMC) technology, providing real-time bidirectional impedance control and advanced power flow control without a high-voltage transformer. It belongs to Siemens Energy's FACTS portfolio and replaces the UPFC concept with a simpler, more cost-competitive architecture.

faqs.q: How does CCSC PLUS differ from a Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC)?
faqs.a: A TCSC controls an inductor in parallel with a capacitor. CCSC PLUS uses an MMC-based voltage source converter, which injects a clean voltage with minimal harmonics and can operate in both the capacitive and the inductive direction – a wider and more flexible control range than TCSC.

faqs.q: How does CCSC PLUS compare to modular SSSC solutions?
faqs.a: Modular static synchronous series compensators perform well at moderate line ratings, but their per-phase module count makes them costly and physically large at high line currents. CCSC PLUS is designed for line ratings up to 4,000 A and delivers equivalent or better impedance control at those power levels, with a lower cost per unit of compensation and a smaller footprint.

faqs.q: What is power oscillation damping, and does CCSC PLUS support it?
faqs.a: Power oscillation damping (POD) suppresses inter-area electromechanical oscillations that can destabilize interconnected AC grids, a growing concern as synchronous generation is displaced by converter-interfaced renewables. CCSC PLUS includes a dedicated POD control loop that modulates series impedance in response to detected oscillations, improving transient stability without additional hardware.

faqs.q: Can CCSC PLUS mitigate sub-synchronous resonance (SSR)?
faqs.a: Yes. SSR, SSTI (sub-synchronous torsional interaction) and SSCI (sub-synchronous control interaction) can cause mechanical damage to generator shafts and instability in inverter-based plants on series-compensated corridors. CCSC PLUS uses active dynamic impedance control to counteract sub-synchronous currents as an integrated function of the control system, removing the need for separate SSR filters.

faqs.q: What happens during a grid fault (N-1 event)?
faqs.a: CCSC PLUS includes an emergency dispatch mode that can be activated automatically or by the TSO on detection of an N-1 contingency, such as the loss of a parallel line. In this mode the system maximizes power flow on the remaining circuit within its thermal rating, maintaining supply security and reducing the risk of cascading outages.

faqs.q: Is CCSC PLUS part of Siemens Energy's FACTS portfolio?
faqs.a: Yes. CCSC PLUS sits within Siemens Energy's Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) portfolio, alongside SVC PLUS® (STATCOM), SVC PLUS® FS (E-STATCOM), Fixed Series Capacitors (FSC), synchronous condensers and mechanically switched capacitors (MSC/MSCDN). The converter technology is derived directly from the SVC PLUS® platform.

faqs.q: What voltage and current levels does CCSC PLUS support?
faqs.a: The current platform is designed for line voltages up to 400 kV and line current ratings up to 4,000 A, covering the majority of high-voltage transmission applications. Applications at higher line voltages can be discussed with the Siemens Energy engineering team.

items.body:
Converter Controlled Series Capacitors (CCSC PLUS) provide dynamic series compensation and advanced power flow control for high-voltage AC transmission grids. CCSC PLUS is part of Siemens Energy's Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) portfolio. It combines proven series capacitor technology with a converter branch – drawn from Siemens Energy's SVC PLUS® and HVDC expertise – to deliver dynamic power flow control directly in series with the transmission line, with no high-voltage transformer required. The platform is designed for transmission corridors operating at up to 400 kV and line current ratings up to 4,000 A.

Three forces are converging on transmission networks at the same time: demand is rising faster than new lines can be built, generation is moving further from load, and power flows are becoming harder to predict. The result is congestion on some circuits while parallel paths run below their thermal limit.

Growing demand is straining existing infrastructure. Transmission system operators (TSOs) are facing a sharp increase in electricity demand, driven by additional loads from data centers, the electrification of industrial processes, and EV charging. Much of this demand lands on infrastructure that was planned for a different load profile.

The construction of new power lines, or the refurbishment of existing ones, is very costly and time-consuming. Therefore, improving the utilization of existing infrastructure can help mitigate investment costs. Permitting, land rights and construction span years rather than months, so TSOs increasingly need to release capacity from the corridors they already own before committing to new build.

Congestion is no longer an occasional peak-hour event – it is a structural condition of networks carrying large volumes of variable generation:

Fixed Series Capacitors (FSC) and Phase Shifting Transformers (PST) remain key assets in modern grid infrastructure, but neither delivers fast dynamic series compensation: FSC impedance is set at commissioning and cannot respond to changing conditions, and a PST responds in seconds to minutes.

Thyristor Controlled Series Compensation (TCSC) adds controllability, but injects harmonic content that requires filtering and offers only a limited inductive range.

A new class of grid enhancing technology is needed: one that combines the reliability of series capacitors with fast, converter-based control, and that stays cost-effective at the line ratings where modular series compensators become impractical.

CCSC PLUS is Siemens Energy's platform-based solution for dynamic series compensation in AC transmission grids. It builds on the proven foundation of Fixed Series Capacitor (FSC) technology – adding a converter branch in parallel with the capacitor bank to enable real-time, bidirectional impedance control, in both the capacitive and the inductive direction.

Side view of the CCSC PLUS substation connection. The CCSC PLUS is installed in series with the transmission line; the containerized converter branch (VSC) is installed in parallel with the capacitor bank on the same platform

CCSC PLUS is the successor to the Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) concept. Where a UPFC required a high-voltage shunt transformer and a back-to-back converter arrangement, CCSC PLUS is installed directly in series with the line. Removing the transformer removes the single largest cost and footprint driver, while delivering comparable dynamic control capability.

Because no high-voltage transformer is required, CCSC PLUS offers a shorter lead time, a competitive installed cost and a smaller substation footprint than transformer-coupled alternatives – while providing full dynamic control capability.

CCSC PLUS combines two well-established Siemens Energy building blocks on a single line-voltage platform: a series capacitor bank and a containerized voltage source converter. The sections below cover the system architecture, the two control modes, and the additional grid-support functions the converter branch enables.

items.title: Gas-insulated switchgear and busduct
items.description: Siemens Energy offers SF6-free gas-insulated switchgear with clean air insulation and digital tech for efficient, eco-friendly, and reliable power transmission.

faqs.q: What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
faqs.a: Gas-insulated Switchgear (GIS) integrate functions like switching, disconnecting, earthing, measurement and surge protection in a very compact and highly compatible way.

faqs.q: How does gas insulated switchgear (GIS) work?
faqs.a: HV switchgear are stations of a transmission system (grid) where voltage is transformed from high to low or the reverse using transformers. In a GIS substation the switching products are installed in metal-enclosed gas compartments.

faqs.q: What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS) used for?
faqs.a: GIS transform voltages from high to low or the reverse in a grid. Electric power may flow through several substations between generating plant and consumer, and may be changed in voltage in several steps.

faqs.q: What is SF6 gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
faqs.a: SF6 (Sulphur Hexafluoride) is the most commonly used insulation gas in GIS over the last decades, which is the most climate hostile greenhouse gas in the world.

faqs.q: What is the alternative to SF6 gas in switchgear?
faqs.a: To reduce the CO2 footprint in switchgear there are being new technologies developed using alternative gases, such as clean air, CO2, Fluoronitrile-mix, etc.

faqs.q: What are the main components of GIS?
faqs.a: Each circuit-breaker bay includes the full range of disconnecting and earthing switches, instrument transformers, control and protection equipment, and interlocking and monitoring facilities.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of Gas-Insulated Switchgear?
faqs.a: Minimum space requirements compared to AIS substation; metal compartments ensure full protection against contact with live parts and protection against pollution

faqs.q: Are there environmental and regulatory considerations for GIS?
faqs.a: All regulations related to SF6 or other F-gases

faqs.q: What is the difference between GIS and GIB?
faqs.a: GIS = gas-insulated switchgear; GIB = gas-insulated busduct containing one or more busbars (cable connection)

faqs.q: What is the difference between GIS and AIS?
faqs.a: GIS = gas-insualted switchgear; AIS = air-insulated switchgear; same function but different types of installation

items.body:
With the energy sector having a greater carbon impact than every other industry combined, the urgent need for decarbonization to combat climate change cannot be overstated. Renewable energy sources are only part of the solution; at Siemens Energy we understand how essential it is to achieve Zero Global Warming Potential (GWP) in the transmission of power as well as in its generation.

Most switchgear still uses SF6 for insulation – a gas 24,300 times more climate-hostile than CO2 and one which stays in the atmosphere for up to 1,000 years. Even the new F-gas alternatives are still harmful to the environment when released. That’s not sustainable, as recognized by the new EU-F-gas regulation. And it’s why we’ve developed our Zero-harm Blue portfolio, including gas-insulated switchgear and gas-insulated busduct.

Our new customizable 8VM3 switchgear operates at 72.5 kV and its modular design gives it the flexibility to work in conventional onshore substations as well as offshore wind turbines.

The only way to achieve Zero GWP and Zero toxicity is by using clean air. Blue switchgear combines vacuum switching technology with clean air insulation. It operates with Zero harmful greenhouse gases of any kind, with Zero toxic decomposition products and Zero safety requirements during handling and maintenance.

LPITs are innovative voltage and current transformers providing a safe, reliable and standardized solution for measurement and protection applications in GIS.

By combining real-time data acquisition, advanced analytics, and secure automation, Node delivers a holistic view of digital substation health and performance - across transformers, switchgear, AC protection, automation & control systems, keeping breakers, insulation, and gas systems healthy and predictable. Siemens Energy's Noedra Node detects anomalies early, reduce forced outages, and streamline maintenance across your installations.

items.title: Reliable gas turbines
items.description: Siemens Energy develops state-of-the-art gas turbines. Discover our product range – heavy-duty, industrial and aeroderivative gas turbines up to 593 MW.

faqs.q: What is a gas turbine and how does it work?
faqs.a: A gas turbine is an internal combustion engine that converts fuels like natural gas or hydrogen into mechanical energy. It compresses air, mixes it with fuel, and ignites the mixture in a continuous process. The resulting high-pressure gases spin turbine blades to generate power, used in power plants, industry, aircraft, and ships.

faqs.q: What are gas turbines used for?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are used in various applications, including: • Power generation: Producing electricity in power plants • Industrial use (e.g., oil and gas): Driving compressors, pumps, and generators • Aviation: Powering jet engines in aircraft • Marine propulsion: Driving ships and submarines

faqs.q: Who makes gas turbines?
faqs.a: • Siemens Energy • GE Vernova • Mitsubishi Power • Rolls-Royce • Ansaldo Energia • Solar Turbines (a Caterpillar company) • Kawasaki Heavy Industries • Capstone Green Energy • MAN Energy Solutions • OPRA Turbines These companies are leaders in the industry, providing advanced and efficient gas turbines for various applications.

faqs.q: How efficient are gas turbines?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are highly efficient, achieving thermal efficiencies of 30–40% in simple-cycle configurations. In combined-cycle systems, where waste heat is reused, efficiency can exceed 60%. Performance depends on design, size, and operating conditions. Due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and low maintenance requirements, gas turbines are a reliable choice for power generation and industrial applications.

faqs.q: Where are gas turbines most commonly used in the process industries?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are widely used in process industries for: • Driving compressors: Essential for various industrial processes • Power generation: Providing electricity for on-site needs • Pump drives: Common in the oil and gas industry These applications enhance operational efficiency, reliability, and energy performance in industrial operations.

faqs.q: What are the biggest problems with gas turbines?
faqs.a: Gas turbines face several challenges. High temperatures can cause thermal stress, material fatigue, and failure. Vibrations can damage rotors and bearings. Fouling – the buildup of dirt and particles – reduces efficiency. Poor lubrication can lead to wear and overheating.To ensure safe, efficient operation, these issues require high-quality materials, regular maintenance, and monitoring.

faqs.q: What are aeroderivative gas turbines?
faqs.a: Aeroderivative gas turbines are lighter, more flexible versions of gas turbines originally designed for aircraft engines. They are adapted for use in power generation and industrial applications.

faqs.q: What are the main applications of Siemens Energy's gas turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy's gas turbines are used in various applications, including: • Power generation: For utilities, independent power producers, and industrial users • Oil and gas industry: Powering upstream, midstream, and downstream operations • Mechanical drive applications: Driving compressors and pumps in industrial processes These applications demonstrate the versatility and reliability of Siemens Energy's gas turbines.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy's gas turbines compare to those of other gas turbines manufacturers?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s gas turbines are known for their high efficiency, reliability, and fuel flexibility, including hydrogen readiness. Their broad portfolio supports diverse applications, from power generation to industrial use. Siemens stands out for its commitment to sustainability and innovation, making it a key player in the global energy transition.

faqs.q: What maintenance and support services does Siemens Energy offer for gas turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers comprehensive maintenance and support services for gas turbines, including: • Repair and Overhaul • Modernizations and Upgrades • Remote Monitoring • Lifetime Extensions • Digital Services These services ensure efficient and reliable turbine operation.

items.body:
Siemens Energy's goal is to build a decarbonized and sustainable future together with its customers. The SGT-9000HL gas turbine can help you reduce your carbon footprint now while looking to the future, all while providing fast, reliable energy production.

We foster a mindset that explores new technologies to improve high efficiency, low emissions, reliability and flexible operations.

The Sun Ba project in Taiwan was honoured with the prestigious POWER Gas Top Plant of the Year award at the 2025 POWER Awards. This award recognises the project's cutting-edge gas-fired technology, its exceptionally low NOx emissions and its pivotal role in facilitating Taiwan's shift towards a cleaner and more sustainable industrial energy system.

Associated selects Siemens Energy’s HL gas turbine to deliver fast-ramping, high-efficiency peaking power to meet growing peak demand in the U.S. Midwest.

There is not just one solution which will produce enough power and meet net zero emissions targets. A mix of new technologies, including high output and fuel-flexible options like the SGT-9000HL, are paving the way to sustainable energy. Whether you’re switching from coal to gas, to higher efficiency solutions, or to low- and no-carbon fuels, we’re with you on this journey. Integrating with renewables and carbon capture storage technologies are also ways the SGT-9000HL can help you drive the energy transition.

The SGT6-9000HL at Duke Energy’s Lincoln station supports solar and the path to net-zero. Watch the webinar video to learn more.

How gas turbine technology is leading the way to net zero - Article in POWER Magazine

New 9000HL-class gas turbine breaking performance records - Article in Gas Turbine World

In October 2023, we have received the TÜV SÜD certificate for the hydrogen readiness concept covering combined cycle plants, simple cycle plants and combined heat and power plants equipped with the SGT-9000HL. With this certificate, TÜV SÜD validates the readiness concept for main systems and components with exception of the gas turbine package for hydrogen readiness up to 100% hydrogen. The gas turbine package itself is rated as H2 ready for up to 50%Vol, based on current rig test results.

This is an important milestone in the 9000HL’s hydrogen journey as TÜV SÜD is an internationally recognized certifier, and this certificate is evidence that we meet the requirements to offer hydrogen-ready power plants in line with regulatory requirements, customer expectations and transformation roadmaps. We are aiming to have all gas turbines capable of burning 100% hydrogen by 2030, to help our customers meet their demands of the energy transition.

Complementing the HL gas turbine, our innovative GT Auxiliary Integrated Package (AIP) provides you with smart, streamlined construction and servicing.

The Siemens Energy SGT-300 gas turbine is a reliable and proven solution for power generation and combined heat and power applications. With a single-shaft configuration providing an electrical power output of 8.0 MW, and a twin-shaft version delivering either 8.4 MW or 9.1 MW, the SGT-300 offers versatile power generation capabilities.

Its compact design, on-site maintainability, and inherent reliability, combined with its ability to operate with a wide range of gaseous and liquid fuels and to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2), make it an efficient and flexible gas turbine for various applications. To date, over 200 units have been sold, contributing to a combined fleet experience exceeding of over 10 million equivalent operating hours, which demontsrates a class-leading reliability rate of 99.5%.

Do you have a question regarding Siemens Energy products, solutions and services?

The SGT-300 offers low maintenance requirements and reduced emissions. It is available in a single-shaft configuration for power generation and a twin-shaft version for mechanical drive applications.

In cogeneration configuration, with its excellent efficiency and high steam-raising capability, the SGT-300 forms the core of reliable, efficient and powerful combined heat and power plants. For industrial cogeneration, the high steam-raising capability of more than 18 tonnes per hour contributes towards achieving overall plant efficiencies of 80% or higher.

For compliance with stringent environmental legislation, the SGT-300 gas turbine is equipped with a Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustion system, providing low NOₓ emission levels with liquid and gaseous fuels. Emissions on gas fuel, corrected to 15% O₂ dry: NOₓ: < 10 ppmvd CO: < 10 ppmvd

The SGT-300 operates on a wide range of gases, covering an extensive Wobbe fuel range. The engine, equipped with DLE burners, is capable to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2). It also supports numerous liquid fuels and features dual-fuel operation. Automatic switching between primary and secondary fuels is possible at any load.

The SGT-300 can be maintained on-site. Furthermore, the option of rapid core turbine exchange will minimize the downtime of the gas turbine.

The SGT-300's compact design, reliability, and easy maintenance on or off site make it well-suited for the demanding oil and gas industry.

The single-shaft SGT-300 consists of a single twin-bearing rotor with heavy-duty casing. Quick core engine exchange is possible, which significantly cuts your maintenance-related downtime.

The SGT-300 twin-shaft has a 2-stage gas generator turbine and a 2-stage power turbine. The core turbine is designed for high reliability with powerful performance and quick load following. Its modular design approach allows turbine module exchanges to be carried out on-site as an alternative to a gas generator or power turbine service exchange.

Both versions of the SGT-300 gas turbine are equipped with a Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustion system, providing low NOₓ emission levels with liquid and gaseous fuels and dual-fuel capability.

The compact SGT-300 gas turbine packages for power generation and mechanical drive applications comprise factory-tested modules, and offer a high power-to-weight ratio. The packages incorporate gas turbine, gearbox (where applicable), drive unit and all factory-tested fluid modules, all of which are mounted on an underbase. This makes them easy to transport, install and maintain on-site.

The shop-tested and certified fluid system modules are the same for design across the SGT-100 to SGT-400 range and come fully wired into the package control systems:

The health and safety of the operation and maintenance staff are paramount. This is why our SGT-300 packages are designed with a special emphasis on, e.g., walkways and handrails, noise suppression, access doorways, and safety interlocks.

faqs.q: Proven reliability

faqs.q: Excellent performance
faqs.a: With its high electrical efficiency the SGT-800 is the core of your power plant installation – from simple cycle to combined cycle operation, with single or multiple units. faqs.q: What is SGT-800?
faqs.a: The SGT-800 is a powerful and flexible industrial gas turbine from Siemens Energy with a power output of up to 62 MW, designed for a wide range of applications like industrial power generation, oil and gas operations, and combined cycle plants.

faqs.q: What are the main applications of the SGT-800 gas turbine?
faqs.a: The SGT-800 is ideal for both industrial power generation and oil and gas applications. It supports combined cycle, cogeneration (CHP), and grid support functions—whether for base, intermediate, or peaking loads.

faqs.q: How efficient is the SGT-800 in combined cycle and CHP plant configurations?
faqs.a: In a 2x1 combined cycle setup, the SGT-800 achieves a net plant efficiency of over 60%. In CHP (cogeneration) cycles with supplementary firing, efficiencies greater than 92% are attainable.

faqs.q: What makes the SGT-800 environmentally friendly?
faqs.a: It features world-class low emission levels, with single-digit CO emissions and NOx as low as 9 ppm. Low emissions are possible with both gas and liquid fuels, without water injection, and the system meets stringent global and regional regulations.

faqs.q: How reliable is the SGT-800 gas turbine fleet?
faqs.a: The average fleet reliability of core engine and auxiliary systems is 99.1% (2024), attributed to its simple, robust technical solutions and long-proven record worldwide.

faqs.q: What fuels can the SGT-800 use?
faqs.a: The SGT-800 offers maximum flexibility, running on natural gas, Diesel No.2, or dual fuel (with on-load fuel changeover). It’s also capable of burning up to 75% hydrogen by volume and supports high biofuel content.

SGT-A05 gas turbine variants generate electrical power outputs of between 4 and 6 MW for applications such as base load, cogeneration, combined heat and power, mobile power and emergency power. Since its introduction in 1963, over 1,720 SGT-A05 gas turbines have been sold to more than 500 industrial customers in 55 countries, accumulating an impressive 133 million operating hours.

The SGT-A05 gas turbineis fulfilling the requirements of a wide spectrum of applications in terms of efficiency, reliability, flexibility and environmental compatibility.

The SGT-A05 is proven to operate in various challenging conditions and locations around the world, including the North Sea, West Africa, Siberia, Brazil, Alaska, Southeast Asia and the desert regions of the Middle East. The SGT-A05 engine has been shock-qualified to Mil-S-901C, which makes it particularly suitable for areas with frequent or severe seismic activity.

The SGT-A05 is known for its high fuel flexibility, which will accommodate a wide variety of possible application scenarios and requirements. Fuels include, but are not limited to natural gas, liquid fuel (or both) and mid to low BTU gas fuels. Fuel system options include dual fuel, steam and water injection. Dry Low Emissions (DLE) technology is also available.

Thanks to advanced engineering, the SGT-A05 gas turbine provides fast start-up capability: You will have full power available within 60 seconds in all conditions. This includes hot restarts, with no need to go into idle condition. The SGT-A05 engine also offers black start capability.

Three popular, proven combustion systems that enhance profitability are available, based on your needs: - Standard combustion systems operate on liquid or gas fuel - Wet low emissions combustion systems utilize nozzle steam or water - Dry low emissions combustion systems for gas-fueled installations achieve emission levels of 25 vppm NOₓ and 50 vppm CO

The SGT-A05 gas turbine can quickly handle changes in power requirements, making it the perfect fit for decentralized power generation or emergency power deployment.

The SGT-A05 gas turbine engine is an aero-derived engine based on the T-56 turboprop, which is recognized for its reliability and durability in the Lockheed Martin C-130 Hercules transport, E2C Hawkeye, P-3 Orion and other widely used aircraft. The aeroderivative design of the SGT-A05 series engine provides a lightweight, modular product that helps lower operating costs through improved fuel consumption, extended hot section life and ease of maintenance. The trailer-mounted unit is driven to its installation site, requiring minimal civil works preparation. From arrival to site to full power in under four hours, the light, aero-derivative SGT-A05 mobile power unit is ideal for rapid deployment.

The modular, compact design of the SGT-A05 facilitates on-site maintenance, since the modules can be quickly replaced. A direct core engine exchange is possible and can be executed in as little as 12 hours. The proven lightweight industrial design allows an easy and economical transport.

The SGT-A35 legacy spans over 50 years of continuous improvement through the incremental injection of aero engine technology. Over 900 SGT-A35 units have been sold to date, accumulating a service experience of over 50 million operating hours. The SGT-A35 is regarded as a class leader for reliability.

faqs.q: No “hot lock-out” periods
faqs.a: All variants of the SGT-A35 can be restarted at any time following a shutdown from any condition, without any delay due to "hot lockout" conditions. Unlike some of its competitors, the SGT-A35 can achieve this reliably by inherent design. Thanks to its agile twin-spool architecture, the SGT-A35 provides the most robust solution to restoring power quickly when its availability is most critical.

faqs.q: Evolved from proven components
faqs.a: The SGT-A35 is the latest evolution in the portfolio, introducing a synchronous speed variant to the existing highspeed power turbine coupled to the prove gas generator to allow direct drive or geared drive of an electrical generator. The SGT-A35 can also be utilized in mechanical drive applications, making it one of the most flexible gas turbines in its range. Its performance is optimized for hot climates, delivering significantly more power at 30 °C than its predecessors.

faqs.q: Combining the best in the industry for oil and gas

The SGT-A35 package leverages the best designs and know-how of two trusted names in the oil and gas industry to produce superior customer value.

faqs.q: What is the SGT-A35 gas turbine?
faqs.a: The SGT-A35 is an aeroderivative gas turbine that delivers between 32 and 39 MW of power and mechanical drive. It is designed specifically for demanding applications in the oil and gas industry, both offshore and onshore.

faqs.q: In which applications can the SGT-A35 be used?
faqs.a: It is used for electrical power generation and mechanical drive applications in pipelines, LNG plants, FPSOs and refineries, as well as other onshore and offshore facilities.

faqs.q: What makes the SGT-A35 highly reliable?
faqs.a: The turbine has a legacy of over 50 years of continuous improvement and has accumulated more than 50 million operating hours, with hundreds of units in service worldwide.

faqs.q: How flexible is the SGT-A35 in terms of configuration?
faqs.a: The portfolio includes multiple gas generator and free power turbine variants, with and without Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustion, to match different power, speed, and application requirements.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of the 2‑spool aeroderivative design?
faqs.a: The 2‑spool architecture provides high operational flexibility, fast start capability, tolerance to transient loads, and eliminates “hot lockout” restrictions after shutdowns.

faqs.q: Can the SGT-A35 operate on different fuels?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a dual-fuel turbine capable of operating on gaseous and liquid fuels, with automatic changeover and the ability to handle challenging fuel compositions.

faqs.q: Does the SGT-A35 support low-emission operation or hydrogen?
faqs.a: With DLE options, the SGT-A35 can achieve very low NOₓ and CO emission levels, and selected burner configurations allow operation with high hydrogen content in the fuel mix.

The SGT5-2000E gas turbine is a proven, robust engine for the 50 Hz market used in simple cycle or combined cycle processes with or without combined heat and power supply. It is suitable for all load ranges, including peak load. The SGT5-2000E offers outstanding fuel flexibility. It can be fired with low calorific gases or gases containing CO2, H2S, and N2, as well as with crude oil and other liquid fuels with high viscosity.

This heavy-duty gas turbine provides low NOx emissions, even in the part load range. Today, more than 315 turbines have been sold, resulting in a fleet experience of over 33 million equivalent operating hours. The SGT5-2000E series fleet´s overall best-in-class reliability constantly exceeds 99.5%.

Do you have a question regarding of Siemens Energy products, solutions and services?

The extensive fleet operating experience of the SGT5-2000E lets you benefit from best-in-class fleet reliability of > 99.5%. Its robust turbine design is continuously enhanced by high-performance upgrades.

Thanks to its fast start-up capability, you can achieve full load in only about 12 min. With its fast load change capability, in turn, you will meet the most stringent grid requirements for optimal frequency stabilization.

The SGT5-2000E offers dual-fuel capability and excellent fuel flexibility: It can be fired with low calorific gases or gases containing CO₂, H₂S and N₂, as well as with crude oil and other liquid fuels with high viscosity. The engine, equipped with DLE burners, is capable to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2). It provides reliable start-up and changeover between fuels. The automatic changeover from the primary to the secondary fuel can be carried out at reduced base load.

This robust engine is suitable for a wide range of ambient conditions such as cold climates, hot and dry or dusty environments. For hot and dry conditions, we offer these options to increase your power output:

The SGT5-2000E is designed for easy maintenance to reduce outage times:

The SGT5-2000E core engine has a horizontally split casing and two walk-in combustion chambers, equipped with individually replaceable ceramic tiles. This design allows a hot-gas-path inspection without cover lift. The 16-stage axial-flow compressor with variable-pitch inlet guide vanes enhances peak load operation and supports frequency stabilization. The robust 4-stage turbine incorporates the latest blade and vane design for stable, improved performance. The hybrid burners are able to operate in premix and diffusion mode with natural gas, fuel oil and special fuels such as heavy oil and refinery residues. With the Low-NOₓ combustion system, single-digit NOₓ emissions can be achieved.

Due to its external silo-type combustion chambers, the engine even runs on ash-forming fuels like crude or heavy-fuel oil (HFO).

High part load efficiency and quick load changes due to fast-acting variable inlet guide vane.

The gas turbine package for the SGT5-2000E consists of the core turbine, the generator (SGen5-100A-2P) and auxiliary systems. We offer you a standardized basic design with options geared to your specific requirements. By using standard components and preassembly or prepackaging we achieve short installation times, with staggered delivery and early shipment of main components. We group subsystems and install them in separate auxiliary packages to minimize field assembly.

Designed for short installation times, all package piping is prefabricated to minimize pipe cleaning and welding on site.

The package auxiliaries include the air intake system, exhaust gas system, power control center, instrumentation and control, fuel and lube oil system and electrical systems.

Simple and combined cycle power plants, including optional cogeneration, are available. SCC5-2000E plants with SGT5-2000E turbines can reach base load in under 12 minutes, ramping up at 30 MW per minute. Their high load gradients allow fast power adjustments, providing strong peaking capacity and efficient performance at partial loads, meeting emission standards even at lower outputs. These features make them well-suited for competitive markets with changing energy demands.

SGT5-2000E simple cycle power plants are your ideal solution for peak load or standby. They can be commissioned and installed fast and cost-efficiently. The plants enable quick start-ups and fast load-following.

The SCC5-2000E single or multi-shaft combined cycle plants are based on one, two or more SGT5-2000E gas turbine packages and a steam turbine.

faqs.q: Fast start-up capability
faqs.a: The gas turbine boasts excellent fast cold start and hot restart capabilities thanks to the light and stiff rotor with internal cooling air passages, the advanced annular combustion system and the Hydraulic Clearance Optimization (HCO) active clearance control. The SGT5-4000F achieves combined cycle base load within 30 min for hot start.

faqs.q: Excellent plant integration
faqs.a: Extensive experience in commercial operation means that you can rely on proven and validated package and plant concepts that enable early power generation in simple cycle. Projects are implemented quickly. Since no external rotor air cooler is required, this simplifies the plant integration even further.

faqs.q: Evolutionary 3D blading
faqs.a: The engine's blade design is based on proven materials and tried and tested know-how, while incorporating the latest aerodynamic technologies. The first three turbine stages are thermal barrier-coated. Your benefit: long service life and low maintenance.

faqs.q: High fuel flexibility
faqs.a: The SGT5-4000F offers dual fuel capability and tolerates fuels within a wide Wobbe range. You might need to adjust the burner configuration when the Wobbe index of the fuel gas varies by more than ±15%. The SGT5-4000F combustion system is able to handle different fuel compositions, e.g. natural gas with high contents on hydrogen (up to 30 vol%), propane, ethylene and butane, as well as inert gases (N2, CO2, He, Ar, etc.). Furthermore, the SGT5-4000F combustion system is able to run on fuels with higher amounts of impurities, such as hydrogen sulfide (H2S) of up to 4000 ppm. The fuel system can switch over quickly between fuel gas and fuel oil and vice versa.

faqs.q: Power output augmentation
faqs.a: Wet Compression option Wet Compression (WetC) increases the power output by injecting water into the gas turbine inlet. This optional SGT5-4000F feature can be used for peak-load machines to benefit from high electricity prices WetC enhances the turbine performance by reducing compressor inlet temperatures and increasing the mass flow throughout the turbine. Excess fog droplets evaporate in the compressor and produce an additional intercooling effect. Chiller System option The chiller is a heat exchanger, which cools down the compressor intake air in order to increase the gas turbine base load performance. The system can decrease the compressor inlet temperature far below the dew point of the ambience. A chiller system can generate benefits in dry regions, where the high water consumption of other inlet air cooling options is undesirable. Evaporative Cooling option The system decreases compressor inlet temperature through humidification, raises relative humidity and increases the air mass flow, resulting in higher turbine output power and efficiency. Evaporative cooling is the favorable system in dry and hot ambient.

faqs.q: High steam raising capability
faqs.a: With its high steam raising capability, the SGT5-4000F is excellently suited for cogeneration or combined heat an power (CHP) applications, e.g, for seawater desalinationprocess steamdistrict heating For combined cycle applications with CHP, you can use a condensing or backpressure steam turbine, with or without steam extraction.

faqs.q: Proven in commercial operation
faqs.a: The SGT5-4000F entered the market in 1996. Today, more than 380 turbines are sold worldwide, and the installed fleet has an accumulated fleet experience of more than 29 million equivalent operating hours (EOHs). The fleet reliability exceeds 99%.

faqs.q: How quickly can the SGT5-4000F achieve combined cycle base load after a hot start?
faqs.a: The SGT5-4000F achieves combined cycle base load within 30 minutes of a hot start, supporting rapid response to grid demands.

faqs.q: What types of fuels can the SGT5-4000F operate on?
faqs.a: It supports a wide range of fuels including natural gas, propane, ethylene, butane, hydrogen blends (up to 30%), fuel oil, and gases with high impurity levels such as H₂S up to 4000 ppm.

faqs.q: Does the SGT5-4000F support dual fuel capability and fuel switching?
faqs.a: Yes, it provides dual fuel capability and can switch quickly between gas and oil, ensuring flexibility and security of supply with fast transition times.

Four stages of fast-acting, variable-pitch guide vanes (VGVs) will optimize performance across a wide range of operating conditions, improving part-load efficiency and reducing emissions at low part loads, while also enabling high-load transients.

More than 100 H-class gas turbines are in commercial operation, with more than 4.0 million fired hours.

Designed to bridge the gap between traditional fossil fuels and a decarbonized future, the SGT5-8000H offers the flexibility to complement intermittent renewable sources.

The rotor is based on self-centring and self-aligning discs with Hirth serration and a central tie rod. This provides the advantage of enabling rotor maintenance to be carried out on site.

The advanced annular combustion system in the combustion chamber creates a uniform temperature profile at the turbine entry, ensuring high fuel flexibility and reliability of your gas turbine. Moderate firing temperatures enable the use of reliable, proven materials, reducing maintenance and leading to excellent availability.

Light and stiff rotor design with internal air passages allows faster thermal transients and world-class fast cold start and hot restart capability. Combined cycle base load within 30 min for hot start.

On-board valves ensure controlled cooling air supply, to cover the needs of different operating conditions.

The SGT5-8000H package includes the core turbine, SGen5-2000P generator, and auxiliary systems. Siemens Energy offers a standard design with options for customer needs, aiming for quick installation and efficient power generation. Subsystems are grouped in separate packages to reduce field assembly, and the compact design suits limited spaces.

Designed for short installation times, all package piping is prefabricated to minimize pipe cleaning and welding on site.

items.body:
The SGT6-2000E gas turbine is a proven, robust engine for the 60 Hz market used in simple cycle or combined cycle processes with or without combined heat and power supply. It is suitable for all load ranges, including peak load. The SGT6-2000E offers outstanding fuel flexibility. It can be fired with low calorific gases or gases containing CO2, H2S, and N2, as well as with crude oil and other liquid fuels with high viscosity.

It provides low NOx emissions, even in the part load range. Today, more than 132 turbines have been sold, resulting in a fleet experience of over 12 million equivalent operating hours. The SGT6-2000E series fleet´s overall best-in-class reliability constantly exceeds 99.5%.

The extensive fleet operating experience of the SGT6-2000E lets you benefit from best-in-class fleet reliability of > 99%. Its robust turbine design is continuously enhanced by high-performance upgrades.

Thanks to its fast start-up capability, you will achieve full load in only about 10 min. With its fast load change capability, in turn, you will meet the most stringent grid requirements for optimal frequency stabilization.

The SGT6-2000E offers dual-fuel capability and excellent fuel flexibility: It can be fired with low calorific gases or gases containing CO₂, H₂S and N₂, as well as with crude oil and other liquid fuels with high viscosity. The engine, equipped with DLE burners, is capable to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2). It provides reliable start-up and changeover between fuels. The automatic changeover from the primary to the secondary fuel can be carried out at reduced base load.

This robust engine is suitable for a wide range of ambient conditions such as cold climates, hot and dry or dusty environments.

The SGT6-2000E core engine has a horizontally split casing and two walk-in combustion chambers, equipped with individually replaceable ceramic tiles. This design allows a hot-gas-path inspection without cover lift. The 17-stage axial-flow compressor with variable-pitch inlet guide vanes enhances peak load operation and supports frequency stabilization.

The robust 4-stage turbine incorporates the latest blade and vane design for stable, improved performance. The hybrid burners are able to operate in premix and diffusion mode with natural gas, fuel oil and special fuels such as heavy oil and refinery residues. The Low-NOₓ combustion system, single-digit NOₓ emissions can be achieved.

Due to its external silo-type combustion chambers, the engine even runs on ash-forming fuels like crude or heavy-fuel oil (HFO).

High part load efficiency and quick load changes due to fast-acting variable inlet guide vane.

The SGT6-2000E gas turbine package consists of the core turbine, the generator (SGen6-100A-2P) and auxiliary systems. It offers you a standardized basic design with options geared to your specific requirements. By using standard components and preassembly or prepackaging we achieve short installation times, with staggered delivery and early shipment of main components. We group subsystems and install them in separate auxiliary packages to minimize field assembly..

Designed for short installation times, all package piping is prefabricated to minimize pipe cleaning and welding on site.

The package auxiliaries include the air intake system, exhaust gas system, power control center, instrumentation and control, fuel and lube oil system and electrical systems.

We offer both simple cycle and combined cycle power plants with or without cogeneration. SGT6-2000E-based combined cycle plants (SCC6-2000E) have a fast-start capability. You can achieve combined cycle base load within only 8.5 min for start-up until full load with a start-up gradient of 27 MW/min. High load gradients allow for fast load changes. With excellent peaking capability, and high part load efficiency complying with emission regulations down to lower part load, this is your profitable solution for competitive energy markets with fluctuating power demand.

SGT6-2000E simple cycle power plants are your ideal solution for peak load or standby. They can be commissioned and installed fast and cost-efficiently. The plants enable quick start-ups and fast load-following.

faqs.q: What efficiency can the SGT6‑5000F achieve?
faqs.a: In simple cycle configuration, the SGT6-5000F gas turbine achieves about 40.6% efficiency. In combined cycle applications, the plant efficiency can be up to 60.6%.

faqs.q: How fast can the SGT6‑5000F start and change load?
faqs.a: The SGT6-5000F only needs 10 min from startup (turning gear) to 95% gas turbine load. There is a one minute coast in period from 95% load to full base load. The SGT6-5000F achieves ramp-up rates of up to about 52.4 MW per minute, enabling fast start-up and rapid load changes.

faqs.q: What is the reliability record of the SGT6‑5000F fleet?
faqs.a: The global SGT6‑5000F fleet has accumulated more than 15 million operating hours and demonstrates reliability in the range of about 99–99.2%, making it a proven choice for dependable operation.

faqs.q: Which fuels can the SGT6‑5000F burn?

faqs.q: Can the SGT6‑5000F operate with hydrogen or challenging gas compositions?
faqs.a: Yes, the combustion system can cope with fuel gas compositions that include hydrogen sulfide and can typically burn fuel gases with up to about 30% hydrogen by volume, supporting future‑ready low‑carbon operation.

The SGT6-8000H can be easily integrated in single-shaft (SCC6-8000H 1S) or multi-shaft (SCC6-8000H 1x1, 2x1, or 3x1) combined cycle plants.

The proven and validated package and plant concepts use standardization, preassembly and prepackaging to minimize field assembly and the need for piping fabrication during construction. This results in easy turbine installation and a shorter project duration.

The blade design is based on proven materials and manufacturing processes, while incorporating latest aerodynamic technologies. Your benefit: high efficiency and reliability, as well as low outage risk.

Moderate firing temperatures allow the use of proven materials to boost reliability and keep maintenance low.

Additionally, the SGT6-8000H has been optimized for short outages: Thanks to the Hirth-serrated rotor disk assembly and central tie rod, rotor maintenance and de-stacking can be done onsite. The turbine blades 1 and 4, and vane 1 can be removed without lifting the cover for quick and easy maintenance.

The gas turbine is capable of world-class fast cold starts and hot restarts due to the light and stiff rotor with internal cooling air passages, the advanced can annular combustion system and Hydraulic Clearance Optimization (HCO) active clearance control. It can achieve combined cycle base load within 30 minutes for hot starts.

Four stages of fast-acting, variable-pitch guide vanes (VGVs) will optimize performance across a wide range of operating conditions, improving part-load efficiency and reducing emissions at low part loads, while also enabling high-load transients.

Around 116 H-class gas turbines are in commercial operation, with more than 4.6 million fired hours.

With short start-up times and high load variations, the turbine offers low life-cycle costs and helps to meet fluctuating power demands.

The rotor is based on self-centering and -aligning discs with Hirth serration and central tie rod, providing you with the advantage of on-site rotor maintenance. The advanced can annular combustion system creates a uniform temperature profile at the turbine entry, ensuring a high fuel flexibility and reliability of your gas turbine. Moderate firing temperatures allow the use of proven materials that improve reliability while reducing maintenance, leading to excellent availability.

Light and stiff rotor design with internal air passages allows faster thermal transients and world-class fast cold start and hot restart capability. Combined cycle base load within 30 min for hot start.

On-board valves ensure controlled cooling air supply, to cover the needs of different operating conditions.

The SGT6-8000H package solution consists of the core turbine, an SGen6-1000A generator (or optionally, an SGen6-2000P generator), and auxiliary systems.

Siemens Energy offers a standard design with options for customer needs, aiming for quick installation and efficient power generation. Subsystems are grouped in separate packages to reduce field assembly, and the compact design suits limited spaces.

faqs.q: What does a generator do in a power plant?
faqs.a: A generator in a power plant converts mechanical energy from a rotating turbine into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction, supplying power to the grid or local loads.

faqs.q: In which industries are large generators typically used?
faqs.a: Large generators are used in utility power generation and in industrial sectors such as oil and gas, chemicals, metals, and manufacturing, where reliable and efficient on-site or grid-connected power is critical.

faqs.q: What types of generators does Siemens Energy offer?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers a broad generator portfolio that includes industrial generators, heavy-duty power plant generators, and wind generators for onshore and offshore applications, covering outputs from a few hundred kilowatts up to several hundred megavolt-amperes.

faqs.q: For which applications are Siemens Energy generators designed?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy generators are designed for utility-scale power generation in gas and steam power plants, nuclear and other steam plants, and for industrial sectors such as chemicals, oil and gas, metals, and manufacturing, as well as for grids fed by renewables.

faqs.q: What is the SGen series, and what power range does it cover?
faqs.a: The SGen series is Siemens Energy’s family of industrial and power plant generators engineered for robust, continuous operation, covering a power range starting above 25 MVA and extending up to around 370 MVA in specific series for 2‑pole applications.

faqs.q: What makes the SGen-2000P generator series special?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy SGen-2000P series combines a water-cooled stator with a pressurized air system, reaching performance levels typically associated with hydrogen-cooled generators while reducing plant complexity, enabling flexible load operation, and lowering operating and maintenance costs by eliminating hydrogen systems.

faqs.q: Does Siemens Energy also provide wind generators?
faqs.a: Yes. Siemens Energy (through Siemens Gamesa) offers wind generators for all common wind turbine types up to 10 MW, both onshore and offshore, proven in tens of thousands of installations worldwide for high energy yield and availability.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy generators support grid stability and decarbonization?
faqs.a: Their generators can operate as synchronous condensers to provide short-circuit power, inertia, and voltage support for grids with high shares of renewables, helping stabilize frequency and support decarbonization by enabling efficient, low‑carbon power systems.

faqs.q: What cooling concepts are used in Siemens Energy generators?
faqs.a: Depending on the application and rating, Siemens Energy uses air-cooled, water-cooled, and pressurized air-cooled concepts, with innovations like the SGen‑2000P that deliver hydrogen-like performance without hydrogen cooling.

faqs.q: What services are available for Siemens Energy generators?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy provides comprehensive service including inspections, maintenance, repairs, upgrades, and tailored service concepts based on operating conditions and maintenance history to maximize reliability, efficiency, and lifetime.

faqs.q: Where are Siemens Energy generators installed globally?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy generators operate in more than 60 countries, with a large installed base across diverse climates and grid conditions, demonstrating proven reliability and performance worldwide.

faqs.q: How can customers get support or more information about generators?
faqs.a: Customers can contact Siemens Energy’s support team, which is available 24/7 and provides assistance in multiple languages, or request marketing and technical information based on their specific interests via the contact options on the generators product page.

items.body:
Siemens Energy is a leading provider of power plant generators, dedicated to delivering high-performance equipment designed for continuous operation. The SGen series demonstrates a commitment to industrial-grade quality and efficiency, making it suitable for heavy-duty use in challenging environments.

These generators offer reliable and efficient power generation for applications including industrial facilities, large gas or steam power plants, and renewable energy grids.

The product range encompasses generators with capacities exceeding 25 MVA and includes wind generators rated from 0.25 to 10 MW.

The SGen series generators are specifically optimized for industrial applications, offering a robust power range of up to 370 MVA and meeting critical need for high-performance equipment that delivers uninterrupted power. For 2-pole applications of over 25 MVA, the SGen-100A/SGen-1000A series is the optimal solution.

Heavy-duty generators designed for power production are ideal for large-scale operations that require high-capacity performance. The SGen series generators are specifically engineered to meet the demands of industrial and commercial applications, providing reliable high-voltage power solutions that support smooth and efficient operational continuity.

Siemens Energy approaches decarbonization through three methods: shifting fuels, optimizing industrial processes, and improving efficiency. Their solutions help address each of these areas. Interested in how they do it? Watch the video to discover their impactful strategy.

The Siemens Energy expert team specializes in generator maintenance and repair, ensuring equipment operates efficiently and lasts longer. By assessing each turboset's operation and maintenance history, their service concepts are tailored to keep generators running smoothly.

Proven more than 40,000 times all around the world, our wind generators provide maximum energy yield and highest system availability. For all common wind turbine types up to 10 MW, on- and offshore.

Learn more about the Siemens Gamesa Wind Business

The Baltic region is undergoing an energy transition, increasing investments in wind and solar power while integrating with the European grid. To achieve frequency and voltage stability synchronized condensers, or SynCons, are used – massive rotors, providing inertia and thus stability to the grid.

Parallel connected synchronous condensers are mainly used for providing short-circuit power and inertia. They also help to stabilize the network through voltage recovery during faults.

When components need safeguarding, protection systems provide fast and reliable fault detection and reaction. Unfortunately, many installed systems are no longer adequately able to cope with protection tasks.

The SGen-2000P generator series combines proven design features for high-performance operation typically seen in hydrogen-cooled models. Its water-cooled stator and air pressurization enable broader performance and flexible load-shifting. Using pressurized air instead of hydrogen cooling simplifies the plant and cuts costs.

Siemens Energy generators are operating in more than 60 countries.

Do you have a question regarding our products, solutions and services?

For information and questions, our support team is available 24/7 to assist you in English, Spanish, and German.

items.h1: Air-cooled generators for industrial and large power applications
items.description: The Siemens Energy SGen1000A air-cooled generator series offers excellent performance and outstanding efficiency for industrial and large power applications.

faqs.q: Increased performance
faqs.a: The entire SGen-1000A series is optimized for world-class efficiency of up to 98.9% and stability during load changes and flexible operation. They are designed for 10,000 start/stop cycles during their operational life, making them a cost-effective alternative to hydrogen- or water-cooled generators for industrial applications up to 370 MVA.

faqs.q: Modular design for a perfect fit
faqs.a: Siemens Energy specialists have developed a product line that meets key market and application requirements. Using a modular design approach and pre-engineered options, these generators can be customized to meet specific requirements with minimal lead time.

faqs.q: Customer-friendly erection and commissioning
faqs.a: The SGen-1000A series is designed and manufactured for ease of use. Our robust and proven design features pre-assembled components to shorten the commissioning period. The self-supporting structure of the base frame with integrated cover, machine auxiliaries, and exciter set facilitates easy on-site installation.

faqs.q: Outstanding quality
faqs.a: There are more than 1,000 air-cooled generators in operation. Design, engineering, sales, project management, manufacturing and testing experts work closely together at the Erfurt, Germany location. They ensure outstanding quality by using the latest manufacturing technology and process automation.

items.body:
Siemens Energy’s air-cooled generator series delivers a competitive edge, offering power ratings up to 370 MVA with technology proven in real-world operations. With ongoing improvements focused on increasing reliability, serviceability, efficiency, and seamless plant integration, these generators are designed using over 150 years of engineering expertise—dating back to Werner von Siemens’ invention of the electrical generator in 1866.

Efficient generator for industrial applications: 25 - 370 MVA.

Reliable generator for large utility power plants: 180 - 370 MVA.

The entire SGen-1000A series is optimized for world-class efficiency of up to 98.9% and stability during load changes and flexible operation. They are designed for 10,000 start/stop cycles during their operational life, making them a cost-effective alternative to hydrogen- or water-cooled generators for industrial applications up to 370 MVA.

Siemens Energy specialists have developed a product line that meets key market and application requirements. Using a modular design approach and pre-engineered options, these generators can be customized to meet specific requirements with minimal lead time.

The SGen-1000A series is designed and manufactured for ease of use. Our robust and proven design features pre-assembled components to shorten the commissioning period. The self-supporting structure of the base frame with integrated cover, machine auxiliaries, and exciter set facilitates easy on-site installation.

There are more than 1,000 air-cooled generators in operation. Design, engineering, sales, project management, manufacturing and testing experts work closely together at the Erfurt, Germany location. They ensure outstanding quality by using the latest manufacturing technology and process automation.

Mechanical forces from operation and transient events, such as short circuits, are safely transmitted from the stator core to the base frame and foundation via welded-on spring elements. The self-supporting structure of the base frame with integrated cover, machine auxiliaries and exciter set allows for easy on-site installation.

The MICALASTIC® high-voltage insulation of the generator stator coils enables a maintenance-free stator core.

We use state-of-the-art manufacturing technology for high quality and precision.

Thanks to its modular design philosophy and pre-designed options, the generator can be customised to meet customer needs. The generator matches the turbine's performance and provides a margin for operational flexibility.

You can choose between either rotating brushless exciter machines with stationary field exciter and rotating bridge connector rectifier or static excitation using collector rings with power taken from stationary excitation equipment for your application.

Coupling design can be adapted to different turbine types and any manufacturer's turbine equipment.

The proven installation and maintenance concept sets a benchmark in reliability and availability. Professional installation ensures world-class availability and reliability for the entire lifecycle of the generator. To reduce downtime, Siemens Energy coordinates generator maintenance intervals with those of the turbine.

The generators are designed for easy installation. Certified engineers use their commissioning expertise to ensure quick start-up and reliable performance.

Take advantage of close collaboration between the service, engineering and manufacturing teams, supported by a global network of factories and service centers. Siemens Energy offers service solutions to boost efficiency, reliability and availability.

Remote Diagnostic Service (RDS) enhances asset production by transforming data into actionable insights. Employing a proactive methodology, RDS monitors the entire spectrum of oil, gas, and industrial rotating equipment across more than 80 countries to detect potential issues before they affect operations. Siemens Energy is committed to maximizing the availability and reliability of its customers' installed assets.

RDS is installed easily and quickly. It offers fast, secure online help and advanced troubleshooting without the need for a site visit. Rotor dynamic data will be correlated and analyzed with respect to operational data.

items.body:
Innovative mix of proven design concepts with air-pressurized cooling technology for flexible operation, makes this generator stand out from the crowd.

Siemens Energy's latest product innovation, the SGen-2000P series, combines air cooling with water cooling technology. Pressurized air-cooled generators are replacing indirectly hydrogen-cooled machines to significantly reduce plant complexity. They achieve efficiency and power levels comparable to indirectly hydrogen-cooled generators with ratings of up to 560 MVA. Pressurized air-cooled generators are used in simple cycle, combined cycle, and steam power plants, as well as in synchronous condensing applications.

Do you have a question regarding our products, solutions and services?

Combining GVPI stators with water cooling technology enables uniform temperatures and low stress levels to enhance operational flexibility. The proven reliability is greater than 99.9% for more than 1,700 stator windings between 10 and 22 kV with an output of up to 650 MVA. Our fleet leader has over 150,000 operating hours and 3,320 start/stop cycles.

Modern grids require high operational flexibility because of the increased integration of renewable energy sources. Our design supports high ramp-up/down rates and frequent start/stop cycles while keeping thermal mechanical stress in the stator windings low.

Our proven MICALASTIC® insulation system and Global Vacuum Pressure Impregnation (GVPI) technology ensure maximum electrical endurance and outstanding availability.

The absence of hydrogen gas reduces the complexity of auxiliaries as well as the cost of service and operation. There is no need for hazardous operational areas around the generator. Arriving almost fully assembled, the generator is designed for easy on-site installation and includes many provisions for accessible maintenance.

Our generators maintain a high level of common parts across the portfolio (e.g. stator core assembly and rotor). The part and component re-use improves the availability of spare parts and increases the quality in manufacturing and assembling components from our suppliers, at our factory, as well as on site.

The SGen-2000P generator offers an innovative mix of verified design features in operating ranges typically reserved for hydrogen-cooled generators. The water-cooled stator and air pressurization system allow this series of generators to operate within an extended performance range and with maximum load-shift flexibility.

Depending on load demand, the generator is automatically pressurized up to 1 bar (gauge) to control rotor temperature within industry standards.

Water-cooled stator bars minimize thermal-mechanical stresses in the end winding allowing for unlimited operational flexibility across the design power range.

The SGen-2000P implements technology featuring the latest verified design with more than 1,700 GVPI stators in operation across all operating ranges and a fleet-leading water-cooled GVPI stator with over 151,000 hours of operation and more than 3,320 start/stop cycles with no indication of thermal-mechanical stress-related issues. Without the application of hydrogen, the SGen-2000P series offers you the added benefit of unstaffed operation, e.g. for synchronous condenser applications.

Our patented MICALASTIC® insulation system using GVPI is highly resistant to mechanical and thermal stresses while featuring excellent electrical properties.

Our patent-pending load-dependent air pressurization system enables rotor cooling during flexible operating conditions.

The SGen-2000P generator series was designed for simplified service and maintenance. Along with eliminating hydrogen-related generator auxiliaries, various service-friendly design solutions have been implemented. Its components have been tried and tested over decades of operation, achieving a reliability rate of more than 99.9%. To minimize downtime, the maintenance intervals have been aligned with those of the prime mover and now allow for longer intervals between servicing than ever before. The rotor is designed for lifetime operation without removal for service.

Our generators arrive on site almost fully assembled with the rotor installed – a design feature that simplifies the installation process. Our certified engineers have extensive experience in commissioning and help you to achieve faster start-up times and smooth operation. The SGen-2000P is designed for easy access. The many manholes installed allow for the majority of maintenance to be completed requiring very little generator disassembly.

Besides standard inspection scopes and intervals, you also have the option of implementing a condition-based maintenance plan using customized installed instrumentation, component analytics, and a remaining life counter for better predictions. Based on advanced data analytics performed by experts in our network of power diagnostics centers, we can advise you on a maintenance schedule according to your specific operation conditions and needs.

Our reliable and robust generator is the result of our manufacturing and engineering design teams working in close collaboration throughout its development. By applying the latest digital technologies, our manufacturing facilities stepped up to create a world-class product for you with excellent lead times.
