items.title: Medium-voltage direct current (MVDC PLUS®)
items.description: Discover how MVDC PLUS® can transform your grid infrastructure with flexible, efficient, and sustainable medium-voltage DC transmission technology.

faqs.q: What is medium voltage?
faqs.a: Medium voltage refers to the range of voltages typically between 1 kV and 35 kV used in electrical power systems for distribution and sub-transmission. It is crucial for efficiently transmitting electricity over moderate distances and connecting regional grids.

faqs.q: What is MVDC PLUS® and what makes it different from traditional AC transmission systems?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® is Siemens Energy advanced medium-voltage direct current technology that offers enhanced grid transmission capabilities. Unlike traditional AC systems, MVDC PLUS® provides improved efficiency, flexibility, and reliability by combining the benefits of DC transmission with the adaptability of AC networks.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® improve grid stability?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® enhances grid stability by managing complex power flows and reducing transmission losses. Its ability to control voltage and power quality ensures consistent and reliable energy delivery, even in challenging conditions.

faqs.q: Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with renewable energy sources?
faqs.a: Yes, MVDC PLUS® is designed to seamlessly integrate with renewable energy sources, facilitating efficient power transmission and supporting the transition to sustainable energy systems.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® handle power quality issues?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® addresses power quality issues by providing precise voltage control and harmonic filtering, ensuring stable and high-quality power delivery across the grid.

faqs.q: What new features or technologies could be added to the MVDC PLUS® system?
faqs.a: Future enhancements to MVDC PLUS® may include advanced grid management features, improved scalability, and integration with emerging technologies to further optimize grid performance and adaptability.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® improve environmental compatibility?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® improves environmental compatibility by reducing transmission losses and enabling the efficient integration of renewable energy sources, contributing to lower carbon emissions and a more sustainable energy ecosystem.

faqs.q: Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with existing AC grids?
faqs.a: Yes, MVDC PLUS® can be integrated with existing AC grids, providing a flexible solution that enhances overall grid performance and supports the modernization of energy infrastructure.

faqs.q: What are the typical applications of MVDC PLUS®?
faqs.a: Typical applications of MVDC PLUS® include regional grid interconnections, renewable energy integration, and enhancing the efficiency of medium-voltage distribution networks.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® contribute to economic efficiency?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® contributes to economic efficiency by reducing transmission losses, optimizing power flow, and minimizing the need for extensive infrastructure investments, resulting in cost savings and improved energy delivery.

faqs.q: What is the power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS®?
faqs.a: The power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS® varies based on system configuration and application, but it is designed to handle significant power loads efficiently, supporting medium-voltage grid demands.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® handle bidirectional power flow?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® efficiently manages bidirectional power flow, allowing for dynamic energy exchange between interconnected grids and supporting the integration of distributed generation sources.

items.body:
The future of flexible, efficient grid transmission: unlocking the grid connector potential of medium-voltage DC for modern energy ecosystems - an economic, flexible, and powerful solution for medium-voltage transmission, designed to transform modern energy ecosystems.

As energy systems evolve with increasing distributed generation and renewable integration, regional high-voltage (HV) and medium-voltage (MV) grids face unprecedented challenges in power transmission. The omnidirectional power flows characteristic of modern energy ecosystems demand innovative solutions to ensure stability and efficiency.

Siemens Energy medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) technology, specifically MVDC PLUS®, offers a cutting-edge solution to these challenges. By combining the reliability and efficiency of DC transmission with the flexibility of AC networks, MVDC PLUS® empowers grid operators to manage complex power flows and meet both current and future energy demands. This technology unlocks the potential of MVDC for modern energy ecosystems, providing a powerful tool for enhancing power transmission capabilities and supporting sustainable energy development.

The increasingly complex energy landscape presents numerous challenges to regional transmission and distribution grids. Siemens Energy's MVDC PLUS® emerges as the innovative universal solution, adept at addressing these issues with ease and efficiency:

Several factors contribute to the increasing interest in medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) systems, as they offer innovative solutions to modern power transmission challenges:

As markets become more liberalized, the need for longer transmission distances grows, requiring efficient solutions to maintain power quality and grid stability.

The rise of distributed power generation units introduces power quality and grid stability issues, necessitating advanced technologies to manage these complexities.

To accommodate the volatile demand for flexible electricity supply, grid infrastructure must be expanded, upgraded, and reconnected, ensuring reliable energy delivery.

Distribution system operators (DSOs) require greater transmission autonomy to address the expanded range of tasks in today's energy landscape.

Find out how MVDC PLUS® can help to tackle your grid challenges

Find out more about MVDC PLUS® applications

Siemens Energy MVDC PLUS® is the solution to transmission challenges. It is the efficient, robust, reliable, and compact solution designed to tackle the challenges faced by regional high-voltage transmission networks and medium-voltage distribution grids. By integrating the advantages of DC technology into AC networks, MVDC PLUS® enhances transmission capabilities, strengthens grid infrastructure, minimizes losses, and provides reactive power compensation and load flow control. This technology empowers grid operators to meet the demands of modern energy systems, supporting sustainable and flexible electricity supply.

MVDC PLUS® is engineered with Siemens Energy proven multilevel voltage-sourced converter technology, available in three standardized type ratings. This ensures universal applicability and delivers numerous benefits across diverse power transmission applications.

MVDC PLUS® excels in grid coupling, effectively connecting or re-connecting islanded grids with independent frequencies to larger supply structures, enhancing overall grid integration.

It enables substantial and sustainable capacity improvements, helping to avert or delay costly network expansions by optimizing existing infrastructure.

MVDC PLUS® requires minimal space and supports the use of less visually intrusive MV overhead transmission lines (OHLs), facilitating the transmission of up to 150 MW with reduced environmental impact compared to traditional AC solutions.

Offering an exceptional price/performance ratio, MVDC PLUS® covers a wide performance spectrum, eliminating the need for multiple individual measures and delivering cost-effective solutions for modern energy systems.

MVDC technology is versatile and suitable for a wide range of applications, enhancing efficiency and reliability across various sectors:

items.body:
Integrating renewable energy sources and decarbonizing existing electricity infrastructure are key to meeting society’s energy needs while fighting climate change. Yet, these contributions to more carbon-neutral energy take place in remote areas often hundreds or even thousands of kilometers away from the centers of consumption. Effective solutions are vital to connecting all distributed power generation sources to the grid to make electricity available where it is really needed.

Siemens Energy supplies a comprehensive range of reliable, efficient, and proven transmission systems as grid access solutions that meet and master these challenges.

Renewables such as wind power (on- and offshore) play an increasingly important role in the energy mix and contribute considerably to the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions. This includes wind turbines and complete grid access solutions in HVAC and HVDC technology as well as monitoring and control solutions and operation and maintenance services.

Siemens Energy's HVDC and HVAC grid access and power supply solutions have proven their superior performance, reliability and availability in numerous projects all over the world - in the harshest climates.

Floating offshore wind opens the door to larger and deeper offshore areas with higher wind potential. Siemens Energy offers optimum floating substation solutions for the connection of floating offshore windfarms to the grid or floating power from shore to open the next frontier for renewables. This swiftly-advancing energy transition demands major changes to power grids, making it crucial to stabilize existing, strained grids to ensure continuously reliable operation. items.title: Grid ancillary solutions
items.description: Power stations equipped with black start capabilities and synchronous condensers supplying short circuit power ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control.
items.body:
Modern energy systems are being impacted by the reduction of nuclear and fossil power generation as well as the increase of renewable power generation. These factors can cause stability problems in the HV-grid (reduction of short circuit power/ inertia and voltage dip stability) which might result in a blackout. In order to prevent this, power stations with black start capabilities are required, while synchronous condensers can supply power during short circuits, and ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control.

Siemens Energy offers a Synchronous condenser to stabilize the frequency and support the voltage also for long distances. They could generate electricity during dynamic peak demands and have the capability to build up the grid after black-out. The solution allows to utilize existing assets and therefore offers a very short Return on Investment (ROI)

A synchronous condenser is a generator without a prime mover from a gas or steam turbine. It stabilizes the grid in changing reactive power demands. The rotating mass and the dynamic generation of reactive power stands for the high advantages of this product. The main benefits of a synchronous condenser are frequency stabilization and power supply during short circuits.

Any existing power plant generator type can be converted into a synchronous condenser. It can supply the grid with short circuit power and ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control. Synchronous condensers are designed to stabilize frequency and maintain voltage even over long distances.

They can generate electricity during dynamic peak demands and are able to build up the grid after a black-out. The project time for converting a plant is usually less than 12 months. The solution allows the use of existing assets and offers a very short return on investment (ROI).

items.title: Electrostatic precipitators
items.description: High efficiency electrostatic precipitators for power plants deliver reliable dust removal and flue gas particulate control to support strict emission limits.
items.body:
Power plants face numerous challenges, including stringent environmental regulations, the need for efficient emissions control, and the pressure to reduce operational costs while maintaining performance. One significant issue is the management of particulate matter emissions, which can harm air quality and public health.

Electrostatic precipitators (ESPs) play a crucial role in addressing this challenge by collecting dust from the flue gas produced by boilers and other components. They support air pollution control not only at thermal power plants but also at various industrial facilities.

Siemens Energy offers suitable technologies tailored for plant applications and operations, combining compact design with high efficiency. By implementing ESP technology, Siemens Energy helps power plants minimize their environmental impact while enhancing operational efficiency, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable energy future.

A high voltage is applied to the discharge electrode, generating a corona discharge that produces negative ions. The electrically charged dust is accumulated on the collecting electrode by an electrical field. The accumulated dust is removed by rapping hammer (dry ESP), scraping brush (dry ESP), or flushing water (wet ESP). The most important consideration in ESP for coal-fired boiler applications is to maintain and increase the collection of high-resistivity dust.

View of the Iskenerdrun steam power plant in Turkey

W1C single phase thyristor – HV power supply for electrostatic precipitator

The operating mode of the electrostatic precipitator ESP (wet/ dry) is governed by the raw gas and particulate (aerosol) conditions. As electrostatic precipitators are used in virtually all process industries, conditions specific to plant processes such as startup/ shutdown operation, load cycling as well as varying gas conditions due to changed fuels/ raw materials must be considered.

Electrostatic precipitator – operation, visualization, data archiving, optimization and diagnostic

The SIPREC ODS application is based on Windows operating system and supports Siemens Energy high voltage power supply systems for electrostatic precipitators (ESPs). SIPREC ODS (SCADA) connects simultaneously to all high voltage power supply controllers for comfortable central operation, visualization and data archiving of measured operating values. SIPREC ODS enables optimization of ESP operation and diagnostics.

Thyristor controller upgrade – HV power supply for electrostatic precipitator

SIPREC C is a thyristor controller upgrade set for the retrofit of existing thyristor controller of different brands. The existing control cubicle with all power components (fused disconnector/ circuit breaker, main contactor, SCR-thyristor stack, CT) and peripheral components (interface relays, terminals etc.) are all reused.

IGBT inverter – HV power supply for electrostatic precipitator

SIPREC I technology representsd the 4th generation of Siemens inverter technology, specifically designed for the kind of high voltage power supply required by ESPs. For new ESP installations, we recommend installing the SIPREC I power supply system consisting of the SIPREC I control cubicle and the SIPREC TR500 T/R set for maximum performance. For retrofitting of existing ESPs, we also offer the SIPREC I Hybrid IGBT control cubicle for the reuse of existing and suitable 50Hz/60Hz T/R sets.

items.description: Marine solutions and products from Siemens for automating and controlling the operation of vessels: Safety and efficiency have top priority for us.
items.body:
Safety and efficiency are our top priorities in vessel automation. Our advanced solutions ensure continuous monitoring and reliable control of all onboard processes. They optimize operations and eliminate potential faults through a standardized automation concept. Simplified system overviews provide the crew with a solid decision-making basis under all circumstances​.

We offer state-of-the-art automation and control technology that assists crews in tackling ever more complex technical processes on board – and for almost any kind of vessel.

SISHIP EcoMAIN assists you with ship management decisions by providing operating data from all relevant onboard systems and equipment on a joint data platform.

As a monitoring system, SISHIP IMAC provides clear visualization and seamless monitoring of a large number of fully automated processes running in parallel on ships of all types and sizes.

OBTS and LBTS provide training in operational situations under realistic conditions on the actual automation software – either as onboard training (OBTS), or as land-based training (LBTS).

Our engineering, monitoring, and control system EMCS has been developed to ensure efficient and safe operation of all vital subsystems of submarines.

IPMS, Siemens Energy's integrated automation system for naval surface vessels, features redundant monitoring and control of the propulsion system and other onboard subsystems.

As a ship owner or ship operator, you rely on numerous software and hardware systems to answer ever more complex challenges in your daily business. With SISHIP EcoMAIN, you can use data from any number of systems on board in a uniform platform to make better decisions and save costs.

SISHIP EcoMAIN assists you with ship management decisions by providing operating data from all relevant onboard systems and equipment on a joint data platform that can also be accessed onshore. This allows you to compare important operating parameters across an entire fleet, and to identify and implement best practices that will significantly reduce your costs.

Energy consumption, emissions, bunkering fluids, service schedules, documentation and information management – these are just some of the processes that are typically evaluated and analyzed for optimization.

The powerful and reliable SISHIP IMAC control system assumes all alarm, monitoring, and control functions. Its particular strengths are demonstrated in its ability to be scalable and to process a high number of measuring points. SISHIP IMAC communicates with other automation systems on board and enables the integration of complex systems such as the propulsion control system or the power management system.

The integrated monitoring, alarm, and control system SISHIP IMAC has been developed to meet the highest requirements in terms of operability, safety, and reliability. As a monitoring system, SISHIP IMAC allows clear visualization and seamless monitoring of a large number of fully automated processes running in parallel on ships of all types and sizes.

With every technological advance, machinery and processes become more complex, requiring automation systems even for routine tasks. Therefore, periodic onshore and offshore training supports your crew in preserving the highest levels of security and efficiency by maintaining a comprehensive understanding of real-life situations and how they are presented in the automation systems​.

The OBTS and LBTS training systems teach your crew how to fully exploit the potential of onboard automation solutions. OBTS and LBTS provide training in operational situations under realistic conditions on the actual automation software – either as onboard training in regular operation, by switching between operating and training modes (OBTS), or as land-based training at special training centers (LBTS). The hands-on trainings simulate physical processes and system behavior with mathematical models and the same automation software and HMI that the crew uses on board.

A submarine is a highly complex system comprising a variety of subsystems. Among other things, the trim, regulation, pressure, and ventilation systems must be controlled and monitored. To simplify operation and further support the operator, all systems are controlled and monitored using one central system.

The engineering, monitoring, and control system EMCS has been developed to ensure efficient and safe operation of all vital subsystems of submarines. EMCS combines all onboard subsystems of a submarine in a central, highly functional solution and creates the process transparency required for fast and profound decisions. It shares the operation, control, and monitoring of all subsystems with central and local user terminals and displays all process data in real time on the monitor, affording the crew an excellent overview. To guarantee maximum safety, plausibility checks on the crew’s inputs are carried out automatically before execution. The system factors into the verification the submarine’s prevailing operating mode, e.g. surface navigation, underwater navigation, or silent running. In addition, the continuous monitoring of hardware and software is conducted by a wide spectrum of integrated test functions.

Automation solutions on board navy surface vessels must safeguard the ship and crew in any operating situation, therefore unconditional system availability is just as important as excellent reliability and straightforward operation. IPMS ensures that operations run smoothly and that system failures do not turn into a catastrophe.

Unconditional system availability is one of the primary requirements of an integrated automation system for naval surface vessels, especially when it comes to reliability of the onboard power supply. IPMS, Siemens Energy’s integrated automation system monitors and controls all the power modules, from the diesel engine and gas turbine to the transmission and pumps right through to the exhaust system, including ancillary modules such as fuel supply, ventilation, and fire alarm systems. Its integrated energy management capability ensures reliable power supply and energy distribution in every situation.​

items.title: Expansion Turbines
items.h1: Expansion turbines: integrally geared radial expanders
items.description: Integrally geared radial expanders (expansion turbines) are applied where energy can be recovered from off-gas or process gas streams from chemical and other industrial processes.

faqs.q: What is an expansion turbine?
faqs.a: An expansion turbine is a device that converts the energy of high-pressure gas into mechanical work by expanding the gas through a turbine.

faqs.q: How does an expansion turbine work?
faqs.a: It works by allowing pressurized gas to expand through a turbine, causing the turbine to spin and generate power, while cooling the gas in the process.

faqs.q: What is the efficiency of a expansion turbine?
faqs.a: Efficiency typically ranges from 70% to 90%, depending on design, operating conditions, and application.

faqs.q: What are the different types of expansion turbines?
faqs.a: Common types include: Radial or axial expandersOil-bearing or magnetic-bearing expandersGenerator-loaded or compressor-loaded expanders

faqs.q: What is the difference between turbine and turbo expander?
faqs.a: A turbine generally extracts energy from steam or combustion gases, while a turbo expander is specifically designed to recover energy from expanding gases, often in cryogenic or high-pressure applications.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of using Siemens Energy’s expansion turbines compared to traditional solutions?
faqs.a: We offer: High efficiency and reliabilityAdvanced digital monitoringCustom engineering for diverse applicationsReduced operational costs and emissions

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy expansion turbines contribute to carbon capture and decarbonization?
faqs.a: They enable energy recovery and cooling in gas separation processes, supporting carbon capture, natural gas processing, and low-emission operations.

faqs.q: What industries benefit most from the integration of expansion turbines?
faqs.a: Industries include: Oil & GasPetrochemicalsIndustrial gasesPower generationCarbon capture and storage (CCS)

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy ensure the reliability and efficiency of their expansion turbines?
faqs.a: Through: Precision engineeringRobust materialsReal-time performance monitoringGlobal service and support network

items.body:
Integrally geared radial expanders are applied where energy can be recovered from medium to high temperature off-gas or process gas streams from chemical and other industrial processes. The design is based on Siemens Energy’s integrally geared centrifugal compressor concept invented more than 70 years ago.

Energy in the hot gas stream is converted directly to mechanical energy which can then be used to drive a compressor or generator respectively. While improving the overall energy balance of the plant, this also saves operating expenses as well as capital cost because there is no need for additional heat exchangers and steam generation equipment otherwise required for heat transfer.

Radial expanders can be configured as stand-alone units with up to three expansion stages arranged around a central bull gear, or they can be integrated into the casing of an integrally geared compressor transferring power directly to the compressor bull gear by a pinion shaft.

Radial expanders can be integrated with the driven equipment and auxiliaries into easy to handle packages for ease of on-site installation and commissioning. Packages would normally include the compressor, its driver(s), process gas coolers, lube oil system, process piping, and other auxiliaries. Additional drivers can be electric motors as well as steam turbines.

Keep operations running smoothly with Siemens Energy expansion turbine services. From routine maintenance and diagnostics to full overhauls and emergency repairs, the team can support your compressors to deliver peak performance and efficiency.

items.title: Fixed Series Capacitor (FSC)
items.description: Discover a cost-effective way to increase transmission capacity and enhance grid stability on both new and existing AC transmission lines.

faqs.q: What is fixed series compensation?
faqs.a: Fixed series compensation is a technology used in power transmission systems to enhance capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It involves the use of capacitors connected in series with the line to improve voltage regulation and power flow.

faqs.q: What are the fixed series compensation solutions?
faqs.a: Fixed series compensation solutions include the use of fixed series capacitors (FSC) to increase transmission capacity, reduce voltage drops, and improve system stability. These solutions are tailored to meet specific grid requirements and operational needs.

faqs.q: What is a fixed series capacitor (FSC) and how does it work?
faqs.a: A fixed series capacitor (FSC) is a device used in power transmission systems to increase capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It works by connecting a capacitor bank in series with the line, enhancing voltage regulation and power flow.

faqs.q: How does FSC improve transmission system capacity?
faqs.a: FSC improves transmission system capacity by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines, allowing for increased power flow and reduced voltage drops, thereby maximizing the utilization of existing infrastructure.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of using Siemens Energy FSC technology?
faqs.a: Our FSC technology offers benefits such as increased transmission capacity, enhanced grid stability, reduced voltage drops, and improved power flow efficiency. It provides a cost-effective alternative to building new transmission lines.

faqs.q: How does FSC contribute to grid stability?
faqs.a: FSC contributes to grid stability by improving voltage regulation and reducing the transmission angle, which helps maintain a stable voltage profile and prevents voltage sags and swells.

faqs.q: Can FSC be used on both new and existing transmission lines?
faqs.a: Yes, FSC can be applied to both new and existing transmission lines, enhancing their capacity and stability without the need for extensive infrastructure modifications.

faqs.q: What protection mechanisms are included in Siemens Energy FSC?
faqs.a: Our FSC includes protection mechanisms such as metal-oxide varistors (MOV) and triggered spark gaps to safeguard against overvoltage conditions and ensure reliable operation.

faqs.q: Are Siemens Energy FSC components manufactured in-house?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy manufactures all major FSC components in-house, ensuring superior quality control and supply chain security.

faqs.q: How does FSC compare to building new transmission lines in terms of cost and time?
faqs.a: FSC is a cost-effective and time-efficient alternative to building new transmission lines, as it maximizes the capacity of existing infrastructure without the need for extensive construction and investment.

faqs.q: What customization options are available for FSC solutions?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers customized FSC solutions tailored to specific grid requirements and site conditions, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.

faqs.q: How long has Siemens Energy been providing FSC technology?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy has been providing FSC technology for decades, leveraging extensive experience and expertise to deliver reliable and innovative solutions for power transmission systems.

items.body:
The global energy transition demands innovative solutions to address the rising challenges in power transmission. As energy systems transform, the need for reliable power transmission grows, making it essential to find effective ways to increase transmission system capacity and stability. Instead of constructing new lines to meet transmission demands, leveraging fixed series compensation solutions offers a more efficient approach.

Siemens Energy flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) technology, including the FSC, enhances both newly built and existing transmission lines. These solutions are integral to improving the quality and stability of power transmission, ensuring that grids can handle increased capacity without the need for extensive new infrastructure. By optimizing power flow and supporting grid resilience, our solutions play a crucial role in the energy transition, aligning with broader goals in power transmission and sustainable energy development.

Unlock the full potential of your transmission network with Siemens Energy's fixed series compensation solution.

Innovative series compensation technology offers a cost-effective solution for increasing transmission capacities of existing long-distance AC transmission lines, enhancing grid stability without the need for new infrastructure. Siemens Energy fixed series capacitor (FSC) technology has been a cornerstone in improving grid stability and optimizing transmission line utilization for decades.

Transmission system operators worldwide have reaped the benefits of our tailored fixed series compensation solutions, designed to meet specific requirements. Key advantages of FSC include reducing line voltage drops, limiting load-dependent drops, and decreasing the transmission angle. These improvements contribute to a more efficient and reliable power transmission system, supporting the global energy transition and sustainable development goals.

Fixed series capacitors offer a range of advantages that enhance power transmission efficiency and grid stability. By integrating these advanced solutions, transmission system operators can significantly increase capacity and reliability without the need for costly new infrastructure.

Fixed series capacitors effectively expand transmission capacity by compensating for the impedance of overhead lines. This cost-efficient solution allows for larger transmission capacities without the need for constructing new lines, optimizing existing infrastructure and enhancing power flow.

Fixed series compensation plays a crucial role in ensuring grid stability and reliability. By reducing voltage drops at the connection point, it provides system stability for bulk power transmission and long-distance lines, thereby strengthening overall grid resilience and performance.

Fixed series capacitors offer the most economical solution for transmission system operators. Their simple, proven, and robust technology optimizes power transmission and increases capacity. With all major components sourced in-house, Siemens Energy guarantees superior quality and reliability, underscoring its commitment to excellence in power transmission solutions.

The amount of power that can be transferred through long overhead transmission lines is often limited by impedance, which can lead to voltage drops. For decades, fixed series compensation has been the proven solution to maintain a minimum voltage profile and maximize the utilization of transmission lines. Siemens Energy fixed series capacitor (FSC) technology addresses these challenges by increasing voltage at the connection point, reducing transmission angle and line voltage drops, and improving power transfer capability and system stability.

FSC works by connecting a capacitor bank in series with the transmission line to partially compensate for the inductive impedance of the line. This setup increases the voltage at the point of connection, enhancing the overall efficiency of power transmission. The capacitors are protected by metal-oxide varistors (MOV) and, in case of a fault, the FSC is tripped and the bypass breaker is closed. For instant protection, a triggered spark gap bypasses capacitors and MOVs within less than 1 ms. Gap-less solutions are also possible, provided that local requirements match.

Due to the complexity and precision required, Siemens Energy recommends and offers individually designed solutions with fixed series capacitors, ensuring optimal performance tailored to specific grid needs.

Choosing Siemens Energy for fixed series compensation solutions means leveraging decades of global experience in series compensation technology and flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS). Our comprehensive expertise ensures that you receive tailored solutions optimized for your unique grid challenges and operational requirements. Partner with Siemens Energy to enhance your power transmission capabilities and support the global energy transition with innovative power transmission solutions.

Decades of global experience in series compensation technology and FACTS solutions.

Customized FSC designs optimized for your unique grid challenges and operational requirements.

All major components manufactured internally, ensuring superior quality control and supply chain security.

Extensive service network for installation, commissioning, and lifecycle support worldwide.

The fixed series compensation market is evolving rapidly with smart grid integration and increasing demands for dynamic power flow control. While conventional FSC remains dominant, thyristor-controlled series compensation is gaining traction for its flexibility. Siemens Energy continues to innovate with advanced protection, control algorithms, and integration capabilities to meet the future needs of resilient, efficient, and sustainable power transmission networks.

faqs.q: Why are integral natural gas engines important today?
faqs.a: Natural gas compression is a critical component of the oil and gas industry, enabling the efficient transportation, processing, and storage of natural gas across upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors. Among the various types of compressors used, the natural gas-driven integral engine compressor stands out for its unique design and operational advantages. These systems, which combine the engine and compressor into a single unit sharing a common crankshaft, have been a mainstay in pipeline infrastructure since the mid-20th century. Integral engine compressors are designed for mechanical simplicity and long life, which translates into high reliability and efficiency. Unlike separable packages—where the engine and compressor are distinct units connected via couplings—integral compressors feature a single frame and crankshaft, reducing the number of moving parts and potential failure points.

faqs.q: How can I make my gas engine more efficient?
faqs.a: · Regular maintenance – assuring your engine is maintained according to OEM standards is critical. · Turbocharger upgrade – An operator can improve performance and reliability by upgrading the turbocharger, more air equals better fuel consumption. · Ignition system upgrade – better spark, better ignition, better combustion, better performance. · Fuel injection upgrade – through higher pressure injection of natural gas both performance and emissions are improved.

items.title: Grid connectivity
items.description: Discover Siemens Energy's innovative grid connectivity solutions for efficient, reliable, and secure energy integration worldwide.
items.body:
Power grids are essential as they form the backbone of electricity transmission, connecting sources of power generation to end users, including homes, businesses, and industries. A well-functioning power grid is crucial for ensuring a stable supply of electricity, reducing the risk of blackouts, and integrating renewable energy sources, such as wind or solar.

Power grids aren't ready yet for tomorrow's energy landscape. Aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, and the need to optimize grid utilization, along with the integration of renewables, require modernization and expansion of power grids worldwide.

With a broad portfolio of innovative transmission products, systems, solutions, and services, Siemens Energy supports customers on their energy transition journeys and makes sure to bring power from where it is generated to where it is needed.

At Siemens Energy, we offer solutions that enable an efficient energy transfer between regions, helping to cover the increasing energy demand, and securing energy access and electrification, for example of industries and data centers.

To reach climate neutrality by 2050, more renewable energy sources need to be integrated into the power grid. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), 3.000 GW of renewable power projects are waiting to be connected. In total, the grid is estimated to double in size by 2040 (IEA), resulting in an increasing demand in corresponding grid technologies.

We enable the transmission of renewable power, reducing dependance on fossil fuels and promoting a clean energy mix. Our innovative solutions, including offshore grid connections and high-voltage direct current systems, facilitate the seamless integration of renewable energy sources, such as offshore wind farms and solar power plants, into the electrical grid.

Infrastructure facilities, industry, and private households around the world require more and more electrical energy. As electricity demand continues to rise, it is essential to ensure a reliable power supply that can meet these needs.

Our high-voltage substations solutions, including our product offerings, such as transformers, gas-insulated switchgear, circuit breakers, surge arresters and disconnectors and earthing switches, serve as critical node points within today’s intricate power transmission infrastructure, playing a vital role in safely and reliably meeting this demand.

We help to bring reliable energy to remote and underserved areas, thus facilitating energy access and electrification.

Our pre-assembled micro substation offers a one-step transition from high voltage to low voltage, enabling fast deployment and versatile applications. And with a comprehensive range of products and solutions, we ensure that industries and data centers can quickly adapt to changing needs and remain at the forefront of technological advancements.

We enable transmission grids to cope with growing demands, the shift from traditional fossil-fuel based energy systems to renewable sources, and increasing system complexity with our products, solutions, digital offerings, and services. Step by step, we’re making power grids ready.

High-voltage substations, the node points of today’s complex power transmission infrastructure, play a key role in meeting the increasing electricity demand safely and reliably. We provide the entire range of services, technologies, and components that are required for the successful construction and operation of a high-voltage substation of any type.

HVDC is ideal for bridging the distances between large-scale renewable power generating installations such as offshore wind farms and the load centers they serve. In a multi-terminal configuration, the collecting of renewable power can be combined with pan-continental integration of power transmission systems, such as for interconnecting multiple regional or national AC grids.

Integrating renewable energy sources is key to meeting society’s energy needs while fighting climate change. Yet, these contributions to more carbon-neutral energy take place in remote areas often hundreds or even thousands of kilometers away from the centers of consumption. We provide reliable and efficient transmission systems to connect remote renewable energy sources to the grid.

Data centers face significant challenges as power demand soars. We understand the unique requirements of data centers and offer a comprehensive range of products and solutions, ensuring that data centers can quickly adapt to changing needs and remain at the forefront of technological advancements.

Our pre-assembled micro substation offers a one-step transition from high voltage to low voltage for fast deployment in various applications, including remote electrification and EV charging. Key benefits include quick installation, transportability, scalability, cost-effectiveness for underserved areas, a sustainable SF₆-free Blue portfolio, and reliable power access in regions without MV/LV grids.

Decarbonizing the European economy demands a swift and pragmatic policy that addresses both renewable electricity and hydrogen. This paper, in collaboration with Air Liquide, recommends a practical way forward for energy transmission in Europe.

The rapid growth of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and the increasing demand for cloud storage are driving a boom in data center demand. This white paper discusses data center power demands and the technologies used to generate, store, and dispatch this power.

items.title: Omnivise iSER™ Actuator
items.description: Siemens Energy Omnivise iSER™ Actuators precisely control the position of steam admission valves for power generation turbines.
items.body:
Siemens Energy Omnivise Intelligent Self-Contained Electrohydraulic Redundant (iSER™) Actuators are designed to precisely control the position of steam admission valves for power generation turbines. iSER™ Actuators can be applied to any load, specifically for positioning, holding and trip applications. They meet the most stringent requirements for safety, reliability, and ruggedness.

Do you need to improve your steam turbine reliability with lower installation and maintenance costs? Email us to learn how iSER™ Actuators can make it happen.

Many steam turbines are controlled by antiquated mechanical hydraulic control (MHC) systems resulting in control issues, unplanned outages due to failures and wear, and high maintenance costs. In addition, the experienced personnel required to operate and maintain these systems are rapidly disappearing and finding replacement parts is increasingly difficult. The main barrier to upgrading to a modern electrohydraulic control (EHC) system is the exceptionally large capital investment in the demolition of the old system, installation of the new system, and updates to the plant control system. The single largest expense when modernizing a control system is typically the installation of new welded high-pressure piping for the hydraulic system.

The Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuators solve these challenges at a significantly lower cost. Their self-contained design of these electrohydraulic actuators eliminates the main costs of piping installation while providing the precision control needed for operation and increasing the reliability, safety, and flexibility that turbine owners desire. In addition, Siemens Energy iSER Actuators offer advantages over modern EHC systems, including eliminating virtually all leak points, greatly improved diagnostic capabilities, and enabling of predictive instead of reactive maintenance.

The patented Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuator is a linear actuator providing precise position control of valves based on a 4-to-20 mA input current signal. The actuator was designed for the demanding application of steam turbine control and the pumping system was developed by Siemens Energy to provide optimal flow and precise motion control of the actuator, all while offering the redundancy needed for reliable and safe operation.

Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuator is a self-contained hydraulic system. This means that all the pumps, motors, valves, and other components necessary to operate the hydraulic cylinder are attached to the cylinder itself and there is no separate hydraulic power unit or associated piping. It is also a hydrostatic system, so when the actuator has reached the desired position, the motors turn off and the valve is held in position.

The iSER™ Actuator design has been specifically built to provide hassle free operation and full redundancy of critical components. Internally it has a 2-out-of-2 (2oo2) fluid pumping design with two dedicated motors/pumps for forward stroke and two for backward stroke, ensuring fault tolerant operation during its service. The actuator will continue to operate with the loss of 1 motor in either forward or backward stroke.

Electrical supply and power management rolled into one

Power supply demands in the fiber industry are growing more complex. Using smart protection relays, direct online motor starters and energy-efficient frequency converters with fiber-optic networks. The system tracks every switching operation, predicts load trends, and helps avoid costly peak demand charges or blackouts through proactive control.

These are designed to enable power utilities and industries to unlock the full potential of their electrical infrastructure. The pulp and paper industry has already taken a leading role in the closed-cycle economy by making optimal use of resources, integrating waste products into processes, optimizing energy requirements, transforming into a self-sufficient energy cycle, and using digitalization tools.

We know the importance of a flexible steam turbine design and customization. That is why we provide steam turbines with various uncontrolled and controlled extraction options adapted to the steam flow in your process. We can offer the precise number of extractions indicated by your process requirements.

The Yankee drying process is the most common drying method. Small gas turbines are desirable for use in the Yankee process because the demand for hot air is lower compared with the Through Air Dryer (TAD) process. TAD uses heat to dewater the product instead of the conventional mechanical pressing. This produces a much softer paper and reduces the demand for raw material from 8% to 30%, but dramatically increases the drying load. The high demand of hot air means that the implementation of gas turbines up to 10 MW is profitable for the TAD process.

faqs.q: What are the key benefits of using a wind control system for offshore wind energy?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 connects wind turbines, substation automation, auxiliaries and direct marketing through a single platform in a centralized view. It enables easy operation of multiple remote plants from a Central Control Center over the entire lifecycle of your wind farm.

faqs.q: Can different renewable energy sources be integrated into a single offshore wind control system?
faqs.a: Yes, the Siemens Energy Omnivise T3000 control system is designed to integrate multiple renewable energy sources into a single, integrated platform. This flexibility allows operators to manage not only offshore wind energy but also other sources such as solar, battery storage (BESS) and hydroelectric power. Omnivise T3000 is equipped to meet the challenges facing both the traditional and the new power generation landscape. By utilizing the Omnivise T3000, energy producers can optimize their operations, enhance grid stability, and improve overall energy management. This capability makes the Omnivise T3000 an ideal solution for modern, multi-source energy systems, ensuring efficient and sustainable energy production.

faqs.q: What are the primary use cases and applications of offshore wind control systems?
faqs.a: The Siemens Energy Omnivise T3000 control system is essential for enhancing the efficiency and security of offshore wind energy operations. It implements robust cybersecurity measures to protect against threats and ensure compliance with regulations like the NIS Directive and NERC CIP. Additionally, the Omnivise T3000 supports proactive maintenance and condition-based monitoring, optimizing the lifecycle of wind farms while reducing costs. Its ability to integrate energy storage, solar PV, and green hydrogen production enables hybridization, improving reliability and opening new revenue streams. Overall, the Omnivise T3000 enhances offshore wind energy operations, supporting a sustainable clean energy future.

faqs.q: Which offshore wind parks can utilize the Omnivise T3000 control system?
faqs.a: Our Omnivise solutions can be utilized in a wide range of offshore wind parks, regardless of their size or configuration. It is compatible with various turbine models and can be tailored to meet the specific needs of different projects. Whether for new installations or existing wind farms, Siemens Energy provides a robust and flexible solution for managing offshore wind energy operations. Its adaptability makes it an ideal choice for both large-scale offshore wind farms and smaller, localized projects, ensuring efficient energy production across diverse environments.

items.body:
New horizons: As wind power continues to rapidly grow, driven by the demand for clean energy, ensuring reliable and secure control systems is paramount. Offshore wind controls need to be accessible remotely, reliable, cyber secure, and have an extended lifecycle.

Benefit from Siemens Energy's advanced wind control solutions for power generation. Our offerings include Lifecycle management, Hybridization and Cybersecurity – all powered by reliable cutting-edge technology. Learn more about our offerings and get in touch!

With Omnivise T3000, Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive control solution for your offshore wind projects. From the foundation SCADA system to wind park utilities, substation automation (HVAC - High Voltage Alternating Current) and Utility SCADA, Omnivise T3000 integrates seamlessly across your wind park, including the control of onshore substations.

This offers the possibility to provide efficient power balancing, utility control functions, SCADA functionalities, and substation automation.

Control the offshore wind energy of tomorrow with Omnivise.

Omnivise T3000 integrates seamlessly across your wind park.

Download our white paper and learn more about our Omnivise portfolio and how we improve operations for offshore wind.

Our Omnivise portfolio ensures that your offshore wind projects are efficient, resilient and ready for tomorrow's energy landscape. Whether for large-scale offshore wind farms or smaller installations, Omnivise provides tailored solutions that minimize operations and maintenance, ensure optimal lifecycle management and streamline cybersecurity efforts.

At Siemens Energy, we see a partnership - whether for your unsubsidized or subsidized wind farm - as much more than a simple supplier-customer relationship. It goes far beyond placing and delivering an order. It's a close alliance between both parties. We work together towards a common goal and develop the final solution by sharing ideas and expertise at every stage.

Together we are stronger in operating, maintaining and securing your wind park during the entire lifecycle.

Video: Find out how our experts can support your wind control project.

We design solutions with your offshore wind needs in mind. Siemens Energy's Omnivise T3000 is an integrated control system solution for offshore wind farms that emphasizes ease of access, robustness in marine environments, and cybersecurity protection.

Our solutions are designed to manage a range of functions within your wind farm. From monitoring day-to-day operations, to managing utilities across the wind farm foundation, platforms and the wind farm itself, to controlling high-voltage substations both offshore and onshore. Omnivise T3000 is designed to integrate seamlessly with wind farm central control systems, supporting essential tasks such as power balance management, utility system monitoring and substation automation. It can complement your existing wind farm controller or operate as a stand-alone control system. Omnivise T3000 is a step towards more efficient and secure wind farm management.

Our secure-by-design approach keeps your wind farm secure.

Learn more about our Cybersecurity solutions

As wind power grows so does their risk of cyber attacks, making strong cybersecurity measures vital to prevent financial losses, power outages, and reputational damage.

Wind farms must comply with strict cybersecurity regulations like the NIS Directive, NERC CIP, and KRITIS due to their critical role in national power supplies. A secure-by-design approach, considering cybersecurity from the earliest design stages through ongoing operations, is essential. Standardizing equipment and configurations simplifies monitoring and maintenance, while clear responsibility for cybersecurity at each lifecycle phase ensures integrated, site-wide defenses.

With our holistic and secure-by-design approach we enhance you with a better reliability, reduced risks, and ensure compliance with evolving cybersecurity standards, supporting the sustainable growth of wind power as a key component of the clean energy future.

items.body:
Overhead lines are critical components of modern power grids, enabling efficient and reliable electricity transmission over long distances. Siemens Energy offers comprehensive solutions in this domain, combining innovative technologies, durable insulators, and intelligent system management to ensure the robustness, efficiency, and sustainability of overhead line networks.

The company’s broad portfolio encompasses everything from high-performance composite insulators, such as long rod insulators, to advanced line surge arresters and integrated overhead line equipment, all tailored to meet the demanding needs of high-voltage transmission. Siemens Energy’s overhead line solutions are designed to maximize energy throughput, improve line stability, and reduce environmental impact, supporting the global transition toward smarter grids.

The foundation of any reliable overhead power transmission system lies in its core components, engineered to withstand demanding electrical, mechanical, and environmental stresses.

Siemens Energy produces the highest quality composite insulators, specializing in long rod insulators that combine electrical and mechanical integrity. These lightweight, compact overhead line insulators are resistant to pollution, salt spray, UV rays, and pollution, ensuring long-term performance with minimal maintenance. The long rod insulator design, Type 3FL, features advanced silicone rubber housings and boron-free glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) cores, compliant with international standards (IEC 61109, ANSI 29.11, CSA C411.4-16).

These components work together seamlessly to ensure high system reliability, operational safety, and grid resilience.

Siemens Energy supplies the full suite of overhead line equipment, including conductors, fittings, and accessories, as well as line surge arresters that protect against voltage surges caused by lightning strikes, switching operations, or faults. These components are crucial for maintaining line integrity and preventing catastrophic failures.

These components work together seamlessly to ensure high system reliability, operational safety, and grid resilience.

Siemens Energy provides expert consultancy, condition monitoring, and innovative digital inspection services which employs AI-driven analytics and sensor technologies to detect defects, assess vegetation clearance, and generate detailed asset inventories and 3D line models.

Inspection systems such as Siemens Energy' aerial power line inspection and drone-based inspection solutions enable remote, efficient, and frequent assessment of overhead lines. Using multisensor sensors, AI-powered diagnostics, and digital twin technology, these systems detect faults like insulation degradation, encroachments, or mechanical damages early.

Siemens Energy offers digital solutions that facilitate real-time monitoring and management of overhead line assets, helping utilities plan predictive maintenance, reduce downtime, and extend asset longevity.

These overhead line specialist services allow proactive maintenance planning, safety assurance, and cost-effective grid management.

Siemens Energy continuously innovates in the field of overhead power lines by developing next-generation insulators, surge arresters, and remote monitoring solutions. The integration of AI for predictive diagnostics, automation for inspection, and new eco-insulating materials ensures a sustainable and resilient transmission network for the future.

The Siemens Energy Noedra Flow suite drives line digitalization, giving operators continuous visibility into the condition and performance of overhead and underground transmission assets.

By integrating real‑time monitoring, dynamic line rating, ambient‑adjusted ratings, advanced diagnostics, and predictive analytics, Flow turns transmission lines from static infrastructure into transparent, measurable, and fully optimizable systems.

Working seamlessly with the other Noedra suites, Noedra Flow keeps energy moving reliably - enhancing safety, efficiency, and resilience across the transmission network.

faqs.q: What is Noedra?
faqs.a: Noedra is Siemens Energy’s digital framework—the Mind of the Grid—that connects intelligent solutions (from sensing and control to software and advisory) into one ecosystem. It turns grid data into clarity, coordination, and confident action so operators can work smarter and faster.

faqs.q: How does Noedra Flow suite deliver end-to-end line digitalization?
faqs.a: Within the Noedra ecosystem, Flow suite provides intelligence from above the grid, combining live monitoring, advanced diagnostics, and predictive analytics across transmission overhead assets. This turns lines from static infrastructure into visible, measurable, and optimizable systems—and connects seamlessly with other Noedra suites to support safe, efficient, and resilient power transmission.

faqs.q: What are the Noedra Flow offerings and how do they support grid operators?
faqs.a: The Noedra Flow suite provides three key line digitalization solutions—dynamic line rating (DLR), weather & situational resilience, and AI-powered inspections. These tools give operators real-time asset visibility, improve grid reliability, and support faster, data-driven decisions.

faqs.q: What is line digitalization and why does it matter for grid operators?
faqs.a: Line digitalization turns transmission corridors into continuously visible, measurable, and optimizable assets. As renewable integration grows and congestion increases, operators need more than periodic inspections—they need real-time awareness, predictive insight, and proactive maintenance to keep the grid safe, flexible, and resilient. Noedra Flow suite delivers this shift from static snapshots to continuous intelligence so utilities can act with clarity, control, and confidence.

faqs.q: What is dynamic line rating (DLR) / ambient adjusted ratings (AAR) and how do they safely increase transfer capacity?
faqs.a: DLR/AAR uses real-time weather and electrical data to compute line ratings based on actual conditions, not fixed assumptions. Utilities can unlock hidden capacity, integrate more renewables, and improve compliance, while maintaining safety, thanks to continuous monitoring, automated rating calculations, and integration with grid control systems.

faqs.q: How do AI-powered inspections and situational and weather resilience improve reliability?
faqs.a: Advanced inspection detects vegetation encroachment, thermal hotspots, and component defects using AI and high-definition geospatial data, enabling targeted maintenance and faster remediation. In parallel, Situational awareness and weather resilience provides early warnings for icing, vibration, and extreme weather events, turning risks into actionable insights for outage prevention and rapid response.

faqs.q: How does Noedra Flow suite improve vegetation management and inspections for overhead lines?
faqs.a: Noedra Node suite applies advanced technologies like LiDAR and AI to conduct aerial inspections, identify vegetation encroachment risks, simulate tree-fall scenarios, and detect structural defects, ensuring that overhead lines remain safe and operational.

faqs.q: What measurable benefits can line digitalization deliver?
faqs.a: More capacity, deferred capital expenditure: use real-time ratings to increase utilization.Fewer outages: detect and respond to weather/mechanical risks earlier.Predictive maintenance: reduce failures with continuous condition insight.Smarter decisions: dashboards and scenario analysis support proactive control.

items.title: Benson technology
items.description: Steam is an essential element in the energy supply system. Siemens Energy offers steam generation based on Benson® technology or drum-type steam generators.
items.body:
Benson technology is a proven process for large-scale steam generation in power plants. The heart of this process is the once-through principle. Combined with sliding pressure operation, this allows for highly efficient, flexible, and reliable power plant operation. Our Benson technology and our associated Benson license will improve your specific steam generator and, consequently, benefit your power plant performance.

Find out more or contact Siemens Energy for highly efficient, flexible and reliable technology for steam generation

Since 1933, leading steam generator manufacturers worldwide have built Benson steam generators under licence from Siemens Energy. Benson technology is widely used in fired steam generators for steam power plants, with over 1,300 units commissioned worldwide.

Today, the company is focusing on deploying Benson technology in heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs) for highly efficient combined cycle power plants to support the energy transition.

Today's combined cycle power plants must be more efficient and flexible than ever before. They need to:

This is where Benson HRSGs make an important contribution. Benson HRSGs can be constructed either horizontally or vertically and will fit into any power plant architecture.

Benefits compared with drum-type steam generators

The first combined cycle power plant with a Benson heat-recovery steam generator (HRSG) – the 390-MW Cottam CDC, located in Great Britain – was successfully commissioned in 1999. More than 130 Benson heat-recovery steam generators have been commissioned to date or are currently under construction.

Thanks to continuous research and development, Benson steam generators are recognised for their excellent operating characteristics and high reliability. Depending on the specific boundary conditions of your project, we refine and optimise the design of your Benson evaporator. Another priority is developing Benson-specific control concepts, which play a key role in ensuring your system operates at its best.

From 1975 to 2023, Siemens Energy operated a dedicated Benson test rig for conducting thermohydraulic investigations of two-phase flows in evaporator tubes. These campaigns generated an extensive database on heat transfer and pressure drop in Benson evaporator tubes. The Benson test rig was also used to investigate the physical phenomena of dynamic instabilities. All of these findings support the development and validation of Siemens Energy's Benson design software.

In 1925, Siemens acquired the right to use Benson's patent, and in 1926–27 the first large Benson boiler in Berlin-Gartenfeld was built. Siemens improved the technology and developed it as an internationally acknowledged standard for large steam generators. In 1933, Siemens decided that it would no longer manufacture steam generators in its facilities, but would instead award licenses based on its own patents and expertise. This story goes still further:

Siemens Energy manages existing licence agreements for fired Benson steam generators and Benson heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs). New licences are issued exclusively for Benson HRSGs.

items.title: Combined cycle power plants
items.description: With over 64% efficiency, Siemens Energy's Combined Cycle Power Plants (CCPP) utilize advanced gas and steam turbines to ensure flexible output and lower emissions.

faqs.q: What is a combined cycle power plant (CCGT)?
faqs.a: A combined cycle power plant (CCPP) is a highly efficient power plant that uses both gas and steam turbines to generate electricity by combining the Brayton cycle (gas turbine) and the Rankine cycle (steam turbine).

faqs.q: How does a combined cycle power plant (CCGT) work?
faqs.a: A CCPP works by burning natural gas to produce hot gases that spin a gas turbine to generate electricity, then using the hot exhaust gases in a heat recovery steam generator to produce steam which drives a steam turbine for additional electricity generation.

faqs.q: Is a combined cycle power plant more efficient than a steam turbine?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy's combined cycle power plants can achieve efficiencies of over 64% by utilizing both gas and steam turbines, which is higher than using a steam turbine alone.

faqs.q: What is the difference between CHP and CCGT?
faqs.a: Combined Heat and Power (CHP) plants simultaneously produce electricity and useful heat, while Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) plants focus on high efficiency electricity generation by combining gas and steam turbines.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of combined cycle power plants?
faqs.a: Advantages include higher efficiency (over 64%), lower carbon emissions, operational flexibility for balancing renewables, and low electricity production costs.

faqs.q: What fuels are used in combined cycle power plants?
faqs.a: While natural gas is most common, combined cycle plants also use hydrogen, biogas, syngas, diesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), and other gaseous or liquid fuels.

faqs.q: How to design a combined cycle power plant?
faqs.a: Design involves selecting gas and steam turbines, heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), and configuring single- or multi-shaft setups tailored to power output and market frequency requirements.

faqs.q: What are the main components of a combined cycle power plant?
faqs.a: Main components include the gas turbine, steam turbine, generator(s), and heat recovery steam generator (HRSG).

faqs.q: What are the efficiency and environmental benefits of Siemens Energy’s combined cycle power plants?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s CCPPs achieve high efficiency above 64%, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and offer operational flexibility supporting renewable integration.

faqs.q: What configurations are available for Siemens Energy’s combined cycle power plants?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers single-shaft configurations with a common generator for gas and steam turbines, and multi-shaft configurations with separate generators.

faqs.q: What services does Siemens Energy provide for combined cycle power plants?
faqs.a: Services include turnkey plant delivery covering design, procurement, construction, commissioning, modernization, and 24/7 global support.

faqs.q: How does the heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) function in a combined cycle plant?
faqs.a: The HRSG captures hot exhaust gases from the gas turbine to generate steam for the steam turbine, improving overall plant efficiency.

items.body:
Siemens Energy is meeting the growing demand for efficient and sustainable power generation. Our Combined Cycle Power Plants (CCPP) integrate advanced gas and steam turbines to achieve efficiencies in excess of 64%, significantly lower emissions and the flexibility to match output to demand.

With innovative single and multi-shaft configurations, Siemens Energy provides reliable and environmentally friendly power generation for both 50 Hz and 60 Hz markets.

A combined cycle power plant is a highly efficient type of power plant that uses both gas turbines and steam turbines to generate electricity.

But how does it work? By using both a gas turbine and a steam turbine, these plants can generate more electricity from the same amount of fuel compared to a simple cycle gas plant, because it combines two thermodynamic cycles: the Brayton cycle (gas turbine) and the Rankine cycle (steam turbine).

The diagram shows a typical combined cycle plant layout and process.

The plant burns natural gas to produce hot gases. These gase spin the rotor of a gas turbine driving a generator to produce electricity.

The hot exhaust gases are used in a heat recovery steam generator to produce steam.

The steam drives a steam turbine generator producing additional electricity.

While natural gas is the most common fuel, combined cycle power plants can also use a variety of other fuels including hydrogen, biogas, syngas, diesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), or other gaseous or liquid fuels.

Siemens Energy combines technology, experience, and workforce to provide cutting-edge combined cycle power plants. These technologies aim to deliver a low lifecycle cost of converting fuel into electricity.

By utilizing both gas and steam turbines, CCPPs can achieve efficiencies of over 64%.

The efficient use of fuel results in reduced greenhouse gas emissions.

CCPPs can quickly ramp up or down, making them ideal for balancing renewable energy sources.

High performance with low power generation costs to help reduce the levelized cost of energy (LCOE).

At Siemens Energy, we are pioneering sustainable power generation with our advanced gas and steam turbines. Our combined cycle power plants, ranging from about 40MW up to 1,800MW, provide unmatched reliability and efficiency for both 50 and 60Hz markets, tailoring single-shaft and multi-shaft configurations to your specific needs. Choose Siemens Energy for fast, precise power plant development.

We offer a large portfolio of gas and steam turbines for EPC projects (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction).

With a strong heritage in gas and steam turbine technology, we are committed to decarbonization and the integration of renewable energy sources.

Our scope for power islands includes the main components of the power generation system such as the gas turbine, steam turbine, generator, and heat recovery steam generator HRSG).

items.h1: Hybrid power solutions for a greener world
items.description: Decarbonize your independent power supply while ensuring cheap, available energy with a hybrid power solution from Siemens Energy.

faqs.q: What are hybrid power solutions?
faqs.a: Hybrid power solutions integrate multiple energy sources—such as renewables, energy storage, and traditional generators—into a single intelligent system to ensure reliable, efficient, and sustainable electricity supply.

faqs.q: What are hybrid power systems?
faqs.a: A hybrid power system is an integrated energy setup that combines multiple power sources—typically renewable technologies like solar and wind with energy storage and sometimes conventional generators—to deliver reliable, efficient, and often grid-independent electricity supply while reducing reliance on fossil fuels and improving resilience.

faqs.q: Why are hybrid power solutions important for remote or off-grid locations?
faqs.a: Hybrid power systems help overcome limited or unreliable grid access by combining sources like solar, wind, batteries, and generators, guaranteeing stable and cost-effective energy even in challenging environments.

faqs.q: How do hybrid power solutions support decarbonization?
faqs.a: By maximizing the use of renewable energy and reducing reliance on fossil fuels, these systems lower emissions and help customers meet their sustainability targets.

faqs.q: What is the role of intelligent control in hybrid power systems?
faqs.a: "Advanced control platforms, such as Siemens Energy’s Omnivise Hybrid Control, continuously optimize energy dispatch, balance fluctuations, and coordinate all assets for maximum efficiency and reliability.​"

faqs.q: What are the main components of Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions?
faqs.a: Core components may include solar panels, wind turbines, battery energy storage systems, electrolyzers, heat pumps, and smart controllers—customized to each site’s needs.

faqs.q: Can hybrid power solutions integrate hydrogen technologies?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy offers systems that combine green hydrogen production and storage for additional flexibility, clean fuel generation, and re-electrification.

faqs.q: How do hybrid power solutions improve grid stability
faqs.a: Energy storage and smart dispatching smooth out variability from renewables, provide backup power, and enable better load management, resulting in higher grid reliability and fewer outages.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of battery energy storage in a hybrid system?
faqs.a: Batteries store excess renewable power, supply electricity when demand is high or generation is low, back up critical loads, and help balance the grid efficiently.

faqs.q: Are Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions customizable?
faqs.a: Yes, solutions are tailored to client requirements, site conditions, and decarbonization goals through modular designs, scalable components, and digital control.

faqs.q: How can I learn more or get started with Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions?

items.h1: Industrial power plant solutions for efficient on-site power supply
items.description: Independent on-site power supply: Industrial companies with their own power plant power themselves flexibly, reliably and safely. Siemens Energy offers efficient solutions of any size.

faqs.q: Steel and cement
faqs.a: Steel and cement Processing mineral raw materials requires a vast amount of energy. That’s why procuring electricity and heat makes up a significant proportion of operating costs. Entities that supply their own electricity and heat using their own power plant will enjoy significant cost savings. And with a sturdy, state-of-the-art combined cycle power plant, they can also substantially improve their environmental life cycle assessment.

faqs.q: Oil and gas
faqs.a: Oil and gas From production to transportation and refining – the oil and gas business is getting tougher. Increasingly stringent environmental regulations are forcing many players to take action. Companies that invest in state-of-the-art on-site power generation enjoy multiple benefits – by curbing their emissions through the flexible use of available raw materials and also by using technologies that seamlessly integrate into their production systems. We provide you robust mechanical engineering that will operate reliably – even with frequent changes of load and fluctuating gas quality.

faqs.q: Pulp and paper (fiber industry)
faqs.a: Pulp and paper (fiber industry) Whether you process recycled fiber or use cellulose and lignin from the raw material wood, your systems will consume large volumes of electricity and heat. Generate your own process steam with an integrated power plant on-site. We offer plants with combined heat and power (CHP) in all scales to meet every need. That means you can remain flexible and independent over the long run.

faqs.q: Mining
faqs.a: Mining Mining is all about raw materials. When it comes to competition, it is production costs that matter – and energy costs are a key factor. The remote regions where raw materials are extracted are often not connected to public power networks. An on-site supply requires flexible facilities that can deliver power under tough conditions at low cost. Whether it’s for open-cast or underground mining, in cold or hot environments, as a standalone system or a back-up for renewable sources – we will design and build exactly the power plant solution you need to bolster your competitive position.

faqs.q: Chemical
faqs.a: Chemical Safety is paramount in chemical processes, and outages are both risky and costly – so your electricity supply must be totally reliable. This works best if you have your own generating system on-site, which will make you independent of external suppliers and curb costs in the long term. If a power plant also permits heat extraction, all the better – that will make your entire system even more efficient. We build the right solution for you – and integrate it seamlessly into your chain of processes.

faqs.q: Utilities and independent power producers
faqs.a: Utilities and independent power producers The energy landscape is changing. Small gas-fired power plants will be a mainstay of our energy supply system for the foreseeable future. That’s because they can serve as a flexible back-up for renewables, they’re highly efficient and operate reliably, and they can enable regions to function independently. On islands or at remote industrial sites, covering basic load or peak, with or without heat extraction – our industrial power plant solution will perfectly suit your specific requirements.
