items.body:
Siemens Energy and Eaton have partnered to offer a cutting-edge solution that focuses on flexible and repeatable power, enabling the design of data center campuses to meet hyperscaler lifecycle requirements. This innovative approach features modular design, supporting power needs ideal for data centers exceeding 100MW, and is adaptable to various types of data centers, including Cloud, LLM, and AI. Additionally, the power-to-chip solutions cater to diverse customer requirement, allowing for the replication of designs in other locations and countries.

Siemens Energy's data center power solutions ensure efficient and reliable energy supply, significantly reducing deployment times and enabling rapid scalability.

The digital world is expanding, with AI, cloud computing, and hyperscale services driving the rapidly growing demand for data center services. Meeting the substantial electricity demand of data centers presents a major challenge, as grid bottlenecks, rising costs, and environmental concerns pose significant obstacles.

The joint initiative offers a competitive and future-proof solution: an industry-first integrated, on-site power generation system paired with modular data center construction. This approach enables data centers to go live faster, reducing deployment timelines by up to two years. The power plant design incorporates redundancy, eliminating the need for backup diesel generators and reducing CO2 emissions by about 50 percent.

This solution offers investment flexibility and increased ROI by providing a dedicated power supply designed for future upgrades. It adapts to shifts in power density following rack exchanges and employs modular combinations to meet strategic needs, ensuring a future-proof infrastructure.

The modular data center solutions address key strategic priorities:

Grid access delays challenge timely deployment. The solution enables grid-independent, clean on-site power, boosting operational efficiency. With balanced energization, optimized CapEx, and essential equipment, we ensure streamlined deployment and operational independence, maximizing efficiency in both setup and ongoing operations.

Decarbonization is central. Siemens Energy is providing low carbon solutions, including SF6-free power and grid-interactive UPSs, alongside sustainable manufacturing. Hydrogen-ready gas turbines and modular systems reduce emissions, while eco-passport availability and future-ready power options like hydrogen power, HVO, and CCUS help meet company goals and regulations.

Siemens Energy ensure 99.99%+ uptime with redundant gas turbines and battery storage, removing the need for diesel backup. The approach includes essential onsite equipment and balanced energization, enhancing operational stability and reducing the need for extensive testing and commissioning, supporting continuous operations and system resilience.

We offer hyperscalers, co-locators and investors a unique package, enabling them to reduce the time-to-market by up to two years in many places, which leads to significant revenue gains.

Global head of sales, Gas Services Business Area, Siemens Energy

Data center owners and developers have the opportunity to build capacity and bring it online fast, in any location where they have land available that is close to gas, water and fiber.

Global segment leader, Data Centers, Eaton

items.title: Steam turbines for nuclear power plants
items.h1: Steam turbine solutions for nuclear power plants
items.description: Advanced steam turbines, generators, and control systems for both large scale nuclear plants and innovative Small Modular Reactors (SMRs).

faqs.q: What type of turbine is used in nuclear power plant?
faqs.a: Nuclear power plants use specialized steam turbines designed to convert thermal energy from pressurized steam produced by the reactor into mechanical energy for electricity generation.

faqs.q: What is a steam turbine in a nuclear power plant?
faqs.a: A steam turbine in a nuclear plant converts thermal energy from reactor-generated steam into mechanical power, which drives a generator to produce electricity for the grid.

faqs.q: What is the efficiency of steam turbine in nuclear power plant?
faqs.a: Cycle efficiency in nuclear plants depends on design and operating conditions, typically ranging between 33% and 37% for conventional units.

faqs.q: How to increase the efficiency of a steam power plant?
faqs.a: Efficiency can be improved via modernization upgrades, advanced low-pressure turbine designs, heat rate improvements, extended water-steam cycle solutions, and part-load operation optimizations.

faqs.q: What range of power output do Siemens Energy’s steam turbines for nuclear power plants cover?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers steam turbine trains from 20 MW to 1900 MW for nuclear power plants, addressing both small modular reactors and large conventional facilities.

faqs.q: What types of steam turbines does Siemens Energy provide specifically for nuclear applications?
faqs.a: Steam turbine options include the SST-800 (for SMRs), SST-8000 (full-speed for SMRs), and SST-9000 (half-speed for high-power output), along with advanced low-pressure turbine designs for maximum reliability.

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy support decarbonization with its nuclear steam turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s nuclear steam turbines help meet decarbonization goals by enabling efficient, reliable, and flexible nuclear base load, supporting the shift away from fossil fuels.

faqs.q: What modernization services are available for existing nuclear steam turbines?
faqs.a: Services include modernization of steam turbines and generators, heat rate and output improvement, life extension, recommissioning, and extended maintenance intervals for optimal safety and reliability.

faqs.q: What control and monitoring systems are integrated with Siemens Energy nuclear steam turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy integrates distributed control systems (DCS), precision plant monitoring, and advanced instrumentation for reliable, safe, and efficient plant operation.

faqs.q: Which nuclear power plants currently use Siemens Energy steam turbine technologies?
faqs.a: Examples of currently operating nuclear power plants using Siemens Energy’s turbine technologies are Olkiluoto III power plant in Finland, Comanche Peak and Grand Gulf in the US, Angra II in Brazil, Sendai in Japan, Yang Jiang in China.

faqs.q: How are the nuclear island and conventional (turbine) island different?
faqs.a: The nuclear island contains the reactor and primary safety systems; the conventional island includes the (steam) turbines, generators, and balance-of-plant components that convert steam into electricity.

faqs.q: What is a turbine (conventional) island in a nuclear power plant?
faqs.a: A turbine (conventional) island consists of all equipment used to convert heat (typically steam) output from the reactor’s nuclear island into electrical energy, including (steam) turbines, generators, and supporting systems.

faqs.q: What is peak load, what is peak demand?
faqs.a: Peak load, or peak demand, refers to the highest level of power consumption by an electrical grid during a specific timeframe. Peak demand is the difference between the base demand and the highest demand within that period. It usually occurs during daytime hours when electricity demand is at its highest.

faqs.q: What is a peaking power plant?
faqs.a: A peaking power plant, also known as peaker plant or simply "peaker," is a type of power plant that operates mainly during times of high electricity demand. These plants are dispatched alongside baseload and intermediate plants to handle surges in demand or periods when renewable energy supply is limited.

faqs.q: Why are peaker plants needed?
faqs.a: Peaker plants are essential for ensuring a reliable supply of electricity and maintaining grid stability during periods of high power demand or low supply from intermittent renewables. These plants can start up quickly and adjust their output to follow sudden changes in demand.

faqs.q: How many hours do peaker plants typically operate each year?
faqs.a: Peaker plants typically run for less than 2,000 hours per year, and often only a few hundred hours. These plants are designed to operate primarily during periods of high electricity demand or low supply from intermittent renewables, providing additional power to the grid when it is needed most.

items.body:
Peaker plants play a critical role in modern energy systems as rising electricity demand increases the need for reliable peak‑load power. Designed for fast start‑up and high ramp rates, Siemens Energy’s peaking solutions use advanced gas turbine technology to deliver flexible, dispatchable power that matches demand spikes and supports a secure electricity supply.

A peaker plant, also known as a peaking power plant or simply "peaker," is a type of power plant that operates primarily during periods of high electricity demand.

Peak load power plants are dispatched alongside baseload and intermediate plants to meet surges in demand or periods of limited supply from renewables. Peakers typically run for fewer than 2,000 hours per year, often only a few hundred hours.

Modern peaker plants are usually simple-cycle gas turbine facilities that burn natural gas or, in some cases, liquid fuels such as diesel or fuel oil, biodiesel incl. HVO100, kerosene and others. Peakers are designed to start up quickly, allowing for high ramp rates and excellent part-load capabilities.

In many energy markets, capacity payments provide additional income for gas peaker plant operators, supplementing energy sales revenues. These payments help cover the costs of maintaining and operating peaking power plants, making their service financially viable.

Associated selects Siemens Energy’s HL gas turbine to deliver fast-ramping, high-efficiency peaking power to meet growing peak demand in the U.S. Midwest.

With the rise of renewable energy sources, the role of peakers has evolved. Traditionally, peaker plants were used to cover predictable periods of peak energy demand. However, as the energy system increasingly incorporates intermittent and non-dispatchable resources like solar and wind, there is a growing need for capacity that can respond on short notice. Renewable energy generation costs are usually low, so these sources are utilized to their maximum capacity. Consequently, fluctuations in supply have a greater impact than changes in demand.

Modern peaker plants now need to follow supply changes to maintain grid balance, rather than just reacting to demand changes. This blurs the distinction between peaking and load-following plants. Today's peaking and load-following plants must operate at varying loads and for longer hours to manage the variability of renewable energy. They require faster response times and often integrate energy storage solutions to provide immediate power while gas turbines ramp up. Additionally, due to longer operation times, low emissions are increasingly important.

Discover advanced peaker plant solutions designed for today's energy needs. Gas turbines offer quick startups, fast ramp rates, low emissions, and scalable options, ensuring reliable energy and grid stability. Explore the benefits of Siemens Energy high-efficiency peaker plants.

Ideal for multiple daily starts and stops.

Quick response to changing power demands.

Efficient and emission-compliant operation even at lower loads.

Low capital expenditure (CAPEX) with a good cost/performance ratio.

Short timelines for setup due to modularized design and pre-engineered solutions.

Superior simple-cycle (or open-cycle) efficiencies for low fuel consumption.

Minimal harmful emissions (NOX, CO, SO2, small particulates).

High SC efficiencies for low fuel consumption; optional solutions for remote control or autonomous operation.

Siemens Energy offers a range of supporting solutions, such as battery storage systems for enhanced load-change response and black-start capability, remote control systems to reduce on-site personnel or autonomous plant operation, and hydrogen-capable turbines for low or zero emissions.

items.title: SeaFloat Power Plants
items.description: The evolution of open and combined cycle power plants from land to sea: Siemens Energy floating power plants based on SGT-800 and SGT-8000H series.
items.body:
Imagine a world with access to electricity and clean water – a world with less pollution, less noise disturbances and sufficient resources. A tough challenge and also a necessity when looking at the world’s growing population and climate change. But this is the world that Siemens Energy wants to fit in – with SeaFloat, the new mobile floating power plant.

We have taken up the idea of floating power plants and brought our latest, highly efficient gas turbine frames on to floating devices, thus defining a new class of floating power plants. The evolution of open and combined cycle power plants from land to sea are based on our successful - gas turbines series (e.g. SGT-800, or SGT-8000H) - proven steam turbine series (e.g. SST-600, SST-5000) as well as our reliable generator series (e.g. SGen-100A, SGen-2000P).

Mobility, flexibility and no need for land acquisition are the most prominent features which distinguish SeaFloat power plants from conventional land-based plants. These features come along with short lead time due to high prefabrication grade and enhanced plug & play concept as well as reduced overall project investments making them interesting for various applications.

It is possible to electrify remote areas with mobile SeaFloat power plants enabling deployment and development and pushing economic growths in these areas. Being able to provide fast power, countries facing catastrophes such as hurricanes or earthquakes can be supported quickly. Mobile SeaFloat power plants can help to rebuild countries suffering from damaged or destroyed infrastructure, bringing hope to the people and financial securities to banks and lenders.

For more information on SeaFloat power plants, please get in touch with our experts.

Population growthReliable mobile power supplyEconomic efficiencyClimate protection

Mobile AssetEnhanced power densityEfficient offsite manufacturing Risk reduction (e.g. no soil risks)

Better constructability with lower costReduced project risks with plug and play conceptFaster project schedule

A pre-installed, highly reliable combined cycle power plant equipped with a SGT-800 solution in SeaFloat application provides the right answer for areas with lack of space. High investments for land acquisition are not required anymore. The power output is between 150 MW up to 450 MW depending on the different available plant configuration consisiting of our reliable steam turbine SST-600 and the related generators. High efficiency, also in part load, and easy maintenance make the SGT-800-based SeaFloat solution the ideal choice to develop remote areas. They are state-of-the-art solutions for industrial applications. The power plant is pre-designed and available in a plug and play concept. Based on the project-specific boundaries, the SeaFloat solution with Siemens Energy combined cycle power plants may provide major benefits like up to 20% better LCoE compared to reciprocating engines.

Even the world champion of heavy-duty gas turbines, Siemens Energies high-end SGT-8000H gas turbine has been enhanced for SeaFloat application. It is available in 2x1 and 1x1 combined cycle configurations and delivers the highest power density with up to 1,330 MW, with plant efficiency of more than 61%. Together with the SST-5000 steam turbine, the condenser SCon-4000, the generators SGen-100A and SGen-2000P, and our in-house designed HRSG's the power plant mainly focuses on the substitution of older plants such as nuclear power plants and coal-fired power plants without typical brownfield risk. The existing asset can continue operation due to fast offsite manufacturing of an efficient SeaFloat power plant. A comparison of the SeaFloat application with a brownfield land-based power plant under consideration of demolition works and relocation of existing site infrastructure may result in 20% shorter project schedule. It has the potential to reduce CAPEX by 20%, have 25% better net present value (NPV), 5% better IRR and 45% faster payback.

Are you looking for a highly efficient combined cycle power plant but are limited in space or simply need mobile energy supply? Or do you want to replace one of your old assets with a highly efficient combined cycle power plant but you are facing high soil risks or brown field risks? Do you need a robust simple cycle power plant that will cover peak loads under tough conditions?

Rely on our SeaFloat advisory team to help you with business case optimizations and technical support already in early project phases.

The SeaFloat power plants range provides a choice of different sizes of combined cycle based on aeroderivates (e.g. SGT-A35), mid-sized industrial gas turbines (e.g. SGT- 750, SGT-800) and heavy duty gas turbines (e.g. SGT-8000H). Optimized to the project specific requirements in power output, efficiency and load regime all applications can be installed on different types of floating devices such as a simple barge, typical platform (e.g. oil & gas platforms), floating production and offloading unit (FPSO) or Floating Storage Regasification and Power Unit (FSRPU). SeaFloat is the highest form of modularization providing power plants in one piece as a mobile asset or for a permanent installation. With focus on the Oil & Gas business SeaFloat makes fossil greener by utilization of the offshore combined cycle solutions to reduce fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

Our expert Hamed Hossain talked to Junior Isles from The Energy Industry Times about SeaFloat being a solution for our customers who need a power plant on a floating device.

The SGT-800 combines a simple, robust design, for high reliability and easy maintenance, with high efficiency and low emissions. With more than 340 units sold and over 6 million equivalent operating hours, the SGT-800 is an excellent choice for industrial or oil and gas applications.

The SST-600 is a steam turbine designed for operation within speed ranges of 3,000 to 18,000 rpm for generators or mechanical drives up to 200 MW. More that 400 units operating worldwide and have produced more than 16 GW electricity in more than 16.3 million operating hours.

SeaFloat power plants equipped with world-class efficient SGT-800 in combined cycle application are available in configurations for 150 MW up to 450 MW.

Operational flexibility based on actual operational requirements provides a wide field of applications in industrial environments as well as for baseload operation in remote areas. All gas and steam turbine packages are system-tested with dedicated electrical and control modules prior to shipment.

From influencing process conceptual design, to managing risks, and selecting the right applications for your process safety infrastructure, Siemens Energy is the partner of choice in leveraging your investments towards a broader impact in operational excellence. Siemens Energy enables customers to maintain productivity, improve safety and drive for sustainability.

Transitioning field development projects from early conceptual design through the construction phase demands agility, reliability, and predictability, calling for tools with efficient and accurate execution. Designed for both onshore and offshore developments, Oil and Gas Manager is the industry leading modeling, evaluation, planning and decision support conceptual design and cost estimation solution for global application in the oil and gas industry. Driven by process simulation, its collaborative platform captures team knowledge across engineering disciplines and functional responsibilities, integrating named insights into the asset development process.

Process Safety Pressure Protection Manager (PSPPM) is an enterprise-level process safety software application used by oil and gas, refining and chemical process industries for design, rating, and data management of flare and pressure relief systems in accordance with industry standards and best practices methodologies. Process Safety Pressure Protection Manager utilizes a central data repository providing process safety engineers and managers access to flare and pressure relief systems data and analyses in a collaborative environment, ensuring visibility into the adequacy of flare and pressure relief systems and facilitating management of design bases changes throughout the plant life cycle.

Utilizing two separate process safety software programs to manage critical equipment can be time consuming and ineffective for operating companies. Process Safety Asset Integrity Manager (PSAIM) is a comprehensive solution combining Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) and Integrity Operating Windows (IOW) with an Inspection Data Management System (IDMS) to effectively manage the inspection and reliability program of your process plant. PSAIM is the industry leading process safety software for safety critical equipment, corrosion monitoring, fixed interval and risk-based inspection planning and scheduling, and remaining life calculations. Implementing Process Safety Asset Integrity Manager creates an easier and quicker inspection and condition monitoring solution, bringing immediate and invaluable benefits to your process plant and organization.

Keeping your workforce technically competitive in a rapidly evolving business landscape requires an organization focus on competency development. Offering a range of training from best practices courses to process safety software training, our subject matter training will help keep your team current in respective areas of expertise in process safety software and ensuring productivity in our products. From flare and pressure relief systems to inspection data management system and asset integrity management topics, there is a course designed for every personnel in your organization.

Learn more about industry digital transformation and latest product releases referring to process safety sofware.

faqs.q: What is a Dresser-Rand steam turbine?
faqs.a: A Dresser-Rand steam turbine refers to a line of industrial steam turbines that were developed by Dresser-Rand, a company recognized for its expertise in rotating equipment and energy solutions. These turbines are designed for various applications, including power generation and mechanical drive services, and are known for their reliability and efficiency. Siemens Energy has a long history and acquired Dresser-Rand, inheriting its legacy of steam turbine technology. Dresser-Rand steam turbines have a power output range from less than 10 kW up to 25 MW, making them suitable for a wide array of industrial applications. Siemens Energy now services all former trademarks associated with Dresser-Rand and possesses extensive expertise with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) designs. This enables Siemens Energy to provide comprehensive support, maintenance, and upgrades for Dresser-Rand steam turbines, ensuring optimal performance and longevity for customers utilizing this trusted technology.

faqs.q: Is Dresser-Rand part of Siemens Energy?
faqs.a: Siemens and Siemens Energy have a long history and acquired Dresser-Rand in 2014, inheriting its legacy of steam turbine technology. Dresser-Rand steam turbines have a power output range from less than 10 kW up to 25 MW, making them suitable for a wide array of industrial applications. Siemens Energy now services all former trademarks associated with Dresser-Rand and possesses extensive expertise with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) designs. This enables Siemens Energy to provide comprehensive support, maintenance, and upgrades for Dresser-Rand steam turbines, ensuring optimal performance and longevity for customers utilizing this trusted technology.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits/features of a Dresser-Rand steam turbine?
faqs.a: Dresser-Rand steam turbines offer a range of benefits and features that make them suitable for various industrial applications. Key advantages include: Versatile Power Output: Dresser-Rand steam turbines have a power output range from 10 kW up to 25 MW, accommodating a wide array of operational needs. Standard and Engineered Designs: The turbines include standard single-stage turbines designed for pump, fan, and small compressor drives according to the API 611 General Purpose (GP) standard. Additionally, they offer standard and engineered single-stage turbines as generator drives for waste heat recovery applications. Multistage Options: Dresser-Rand provides engineered single-stage turbines and standard multistage turbines for applications that comply with API 611 (GP) or API 612 (Special Purpose – SP) standards, ensuring flexibility in meeting specific project requirements. High Inlet Steam Pressure and Temperature: These turbines can operate with inlet steam pressures ranging from 30 to 139 bar(a) and inlet steam temperatures from 415 to 550 °C, allowing for efficient energy conversion in various industrial processes. Reliability and Efficiency: Dresser-Rand steam turbines are known for their robust design and operational reliability, contributing to efficient performance and reduced downtime in industrial settings. Expert Support and Service: With Siemens Energy’s acquisition of Dresser-Rand, customers benefit from comprehensive support, maintenance, and upgrades, leveraging extensive expertise in original equipment manufacturer (OEM) designs. These features make Dresser-Rand steam turbines a reliable choice for industries seeking efficient and flexible steam solution

faqs.q: What are the differences between single-stage and multi-stage Dresser-Rand steam turbines?
faqs.a: The main differences between single-stage and multi-stage Dresser-Rand steam turbines include: Design: Single-Stage Turbines: Feature one set of blades for energy extraction in a single pass, making them simpler and easier to maintain. Multi-Stage Turbines: Have multiple sets of blades, allowing for gradual steam expansion and better energy extraction. Performance: Single-Stage Turbines: Suitable for lower power outputs and applications like pumps and small compressors. Multi-Stage Turbines: Capable of higher power outputs and greater efficiency, ideal for large-scale power generation. Applications: Single-Stage Turbines: Commonly used in waste heat recovery and smaller generator drives. Multi-Stage Turbines: Employed in demanding applications, including industrial processes and power plants. Efficiency: Single-Stage Turbines: Efficient for specific applications but may not match the efficiency of multi-stage turbines under varying loads. Multi-Stage Turbines: Offer better efficiency across a wider range of operating conditions. In summary, the choice between single-stage and multi-stage turbines depends on the application’s power output, efficiency, and complexity requirements.

faqs.q: What are the typical applications for Dresser-Rand steam turbines?
faqs.a: Dresser-Rand steam turbines are utilized in a variety of applications across different industries, including: Power Generation: Used in both standalone power plants and combined heat and power (CHP) systems to generate electricity efficiently. Waste Heat Recovery: Employed to capture and utilize waste heat from industrial processes, converting it into usable energy. Mechanical Drive Services: Suitable for driving pumps, fans, and compressors in various industrial settings, providing reliable mechanical power. Oil and Gas Industry: Used in refineries and processing plants for various applications, including driving equipment and generating power. Chemical Processing: Applied in chemical plants for energy generation and process steam, enhancing operational efficiency. Sugar Industry: Utilized for energy generation and process heating in sugar production facilities. These applications highlight the versatility and efficiency of Dresser-Rand steam turbines in meeting the energy needs of diverse industrial sectors.

These diverse models within the Dresser-Rand product line cater to a wide range of industrial needs, ensuring reliable performance and efficiency across various applications.

faqs.q: Does Siemens Energy provide maintenance and service support for legacy Dresser-Rand steam turbines?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy provides comprehensive maintenance and service support for legacy Dresser-Rand steam turbines. Our global service network ensures that customers have access to expert support, regardless of the location of their operations. We are committed to servicing not only modern turbines but also very old machines, leveraging our extensive experience and knowledge of legacy systems. This dedication to maintaining and optimizing the performance of Dresser-Rand steam turbines helps our customers achieve operational efficiency and reliability throughout the lifecycle of their equipment.

faqs.q: Can Dresser-Rand steam turbines be upgraded with new technologies?
faqs.a: Yes, Dresser-Rand steam turbines can be upgraded with new technologies. Siemens Energy is continuously innovating our small steam turbine product lines, allowing for enhancements that improve efficiency, performance, and reliability. These upgrades can include advanced control systems, improved materials, and optimized designs, ensuring that legacy turbines benefit from the latest technological advancements. This commitment to innovation helps our customers maximize the value and longevity of their Dresser-Rand steam turbines.

Applications: Single-Stage Turbines: Commonly used in waste heat recovery and smaller generator drives. Multi-Stage Turbines: Employed in demanding applications, including industrial processes and power plants. Efficiency: Single-Stage Turbines: Efficient for specific applications but may not match the efficiency of multi-stage turbines under varying loads. Multi-Stage Turbines: Offer better efficiency across a wider range of operating conditions. In summary, the choice between single-stage and multi-stage turbines depends on the application’s power output, efficiency, and complexity requirements.

Dresser-Rand steam turbines are utilized in a variety of applications across different industries, including: Power Generation: Used in both standalone power plants and combined heat and power (CHP) systems to generate electricity efficiently. Waste Heat Recovery: Employed to capture and utilize waste heat from industrial processes, converting it into usable energy. Mechanical Drive Services: Suitable for driving pumps, fans, and compressors in various industrial settings, providing reliable mechanical power. Oil and Gas Industry: Used in refineries and processing plants for various applications, including driving equipment and generating power. Chemical Processing: Applied in chemical plants for energy generation and process steam, enhancing operational efficiency. Sugar Industry: Utilized for energy generation and process heating in sugar production facilities. These applications highlight the versatility and efficiency of Dresser-Rand steam turbines in meeting the energy needs of diverse industrial sectors.

items.description: With a fleet of more than 60,000 steam turbines worldwide, Siemens Energy is a reliable and experienced partner that supports the decarbonization of industry.

faqs.q: What is a steam turbine?
faqs.a: Al steam turbine is a type of rotary engine that converts thermal energy from steam into mechanical energy, which can then be used to drive a generator which generates electricity or as mechanical drive for pumps, compressor or fans. These turbines are essential components in power plants, refineries, and manufacturing facilities, where they efficiently harness steam produced from boiling water. By utilizing high-pressure steam, steam turbines offer high efficiency and reliability, making them a critical technology in the energy sector and contributing to reduced operational costs and improved sustainability. Whether for large-scale power generation or specific industrial applications, steam turbines play a vital role in driving innovation and efficiency in modern industry.

faqs.q: How does a steam turbine work?
faqs.a: A steam turbine operates by converting thermal energy from steam into mechanical energy, which can then be used to generate electricity or drive industrial processes. The process begins with water being heated in a boiler to produce high-pressure steam. This steam is then directed into the turbine, where it passes through a series of blades mounted on a rotor. As the high-pressure steam enters the turbine, it expands and cools, causing the blades to spin. This rotational motion of the rotor is what generates mechanical energy. The steam then exits the turbine and can be condensed back into water for reuse in the boiler, creating a closed-loop system that enhances efficiency. The design of the steam turbine can vary, with options for single or multi-stage configurations, depending on the application and required output. By optimizing factors such as steam pressure, temperature, and flow rate, steam turbines can achieve high efficiency and reliability, making them a vital component in power generation and various industrial applications.

faqs.q: How does a steam turbine generate electricity?
faqs.a: A steam turbine generates electricity by converting thermal energy from steam into mechanical energy, which is then transformed into electrical energy through a generator. The process begins in a boiler, where water is heated to produce high-pressure steam. This steam is directed into the turbine, where it expands and flows over a series of blades attached to a rotor. As the steam passes through the turbine blades, it causes the rotor to spin. This rotational motion is connected to a generator, which consists of a rotor and a stator. As the turbine rotor turns, it rotates the generator rotor within the stator, creating a magnetic field. This movement induces an electrical current in the stator windings, generating electricity. The steam then exits the turbine and is typically condensed back into water in a condenser, allowing it to be reused in the boiler, thus creating a closed-loop system. By optimizing steam pressure, temperature, and flow rate, steam turbines can achieve high efficiency in electricity generation, making them a crucial component in power plants and various industrial applications.

faqs.q: How efficient is a steam turbine?
faqs.a: The efficiency of a steam turbine can vary significantly based on its design, operating conditions, and the specific application. Generally, state-of-the-art steam turbines can achieve efficiencies ranging from 30% to over 45% in power generation applications. In combined cycle power plants, where steam turbines work alongside gas turbines, overall efficiencies can exceed 60%, thanks to the effective use of waste heat. Factors that influence steam turbine efficiency include steam temperature and pressure, the quality of the steam, and the design of the turbine itself, such as whether it is a single or multi-stage turbine. Advanced technologies, such as improved blade designs and digital control systems, further enhance efficiency by optimizing performance under varying operational conditions. Regular maintenance and monitoring are also crucial for maintaining high efficiency, as wear and tear can impact performance over time. By maximizing efficiency, steam turbines play a vital role in reducing fuel consumption and lowering greenhouse gas emissions, making them an essential component in sustainable energy production.

faqs.q: How to improve steam turbine efficiency?
faqs.a: Improving steam turbine efficiency involves several strategies that focus on optimizing design, operation, and maintenance. Here are key approaches to enhance efficiency: Optimize Steam Conditions: Increasing steam temperature and pressure can significantly improve turbine efficiency. Utilizing superheated steam allows for better energy conversion and reduces moisture content in the steam, which can cause erosion and efficiency losses. Regular Maintenance: Implementing a robust maintenance program helps identify and address issues such as wear and tear, leaks, and misalignments. Regular inspections and timely repairs ensure that the turbine operates at peak performance. Upgrade Turbine Components: Replacing or retrofitting components, such as blades and seals, with advanced materials and designs can enhance performance. High-efficiency blades can capture more energy from the steam, while improved seals reduce steam leakage. Implement Digital Controls: Utilizing advanced digital control systems allows for real-time monitoring and optimization of turbine performance. These systems can adjust operating parameters dynamically to maximize efficiency under varying load conditions. Optimize the Steam Cycle: Analyzing and optimizing the entire steam cycle, including the boiler, condenser, and feedwater systems, can lead to significant efficiency gains. Ensuring that each component operates effectively contributes to the overall performance of the steam turbine. By implementing these strategies, operators can enhance the efficiency of steam turbines, leading to reduced fuel consumption, lower operational costs, and a smaller environmental footprint.

faqs.q: What are the main applications of steam turbines in the energy sector?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s steam turbines are utilized across a wide range of applications, with a strong focus on industries that require efficient and reliable energy solutions. The primary applications include: Combined Heat and Power (CHP): Siemens Energy steam turbines are integral to CHP systems, providing both electricity and useful heat, maximizing energy utilization. Combined Cycle: In combined cycle power plants, Siemens Energy turbines work alongside gas turbines to enhance overall efficiency and reduce emissions. With their versatility and high performance, Siemens Energy’s industrial steam turbines are key components in these critical sectors, driving innovation and sustainability in energy production. Pulp and Paper: Steam turbines are essential for driving processes in the pulp and paper industry, providing the necessary energy and process steam for production Chemical Industry: These turbines support various chemical processes,either ensuring efficient steam generation or as mechanical drives. In oil refineries, Siemens Energy steam turbines play a critical role in refining processes, enhancing energy efficiency and reliability. Oil and Gas: Siemens Energy turbines are used in oil and gas applications for power generation and process steam, contributing to operational efficiency. Sugar: The sugar industry benefits from steam turbines for energy generation and process heating, optimizing production efficiency.

items.title: Industrial steam turbines
items.h1: Tailor-made and flexible industrial steam turbines
items.description: Discover a comprehensive range of reliable and versatile steam turbines for the power output range from 2 to 250 MW.

faqs.q: How does an industrial steam turbine work?
faqs.a: An industrial steam turbine uses high-pressure steam to spin a rotor, converting thermal energy into mechanical energy for power generation or mechanical drive applications.

faqs.q: What are the main parts of an industrial steam turbine?
faqs.a: Key parts include the rotor, casing, blades, steam inlet and exhaust, condenser, gearbox (if required), lubrication system, and various control valves for safe operation.

faqs.q: What factors affect the efficiency of an industrial steam turbine?
faqs.a: Efficiency depends on design features (e.g., steam path, reheat options), steam conditions (pressure and temperature), operational integration, and maintenance quality.

faqs.q: How is steam turbine performance measured and monitored?
faqs.a: Performance is tracked through output power, efficiency, steam consumption, vibration, and temperature readings. Advanced turbines use digital controls and sensors for real-time monitoring.

faqs.q: What safety procedures are important when operating industrial steam turbines?
faqs.a: Critical safety measures include controlled warm-up and shutdown processes, pressure and temperature monitoring, vibration monitoring, routine inspections, and emergency systems to prevent overpressure or water hammer.

faqs.q: What power range do industrial steam turbines cover?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy industrial steam turbines offer a power output range from 2 to +250 MW, suitable for diverse industrial and power generation applications.

faqs.q: What industries commonly use industrial steam turbines?
faqs.a: Industrial steam turbines are widely used in industries using process steam, such as pulp and paper, chemical, oil and gas, sugar and ethanol production, waste incineration, district heating, as well as for combined heat and power (CHP) and combined cycle plants.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of Siemens Energy's industrial steam turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy's turbines are customized and tailormade to exactly meet condition at the customers' facility. The steam turbines are renowned for high efficiency, reliability, flexibility, and availability.

faqs.q: Can Siemens Energy steam turbines support renewable and sustainable energy projects?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Siemens Energy turbines are used in biomass plants, concentrated solar power (CSP) facilities, and CHP plants, supporting sustainable, fossil-free power generation.

faqs.q: How are Siemens Energy industrial steam turbines delivered and installed on-site?
faqs.a: Turbines and auxiliary systems are delivered as pre-assembled modular packages skids for installation. If the single lift concept is part of the contract the steam turbine and generator are assembled on one skid for time efficient and secure installation on site.

faqs.q: Are Siemens Energy industrial steam turbines customizable to specific plant needs?
faqs.a: Absolutely. The design is highly modular, allowing for various configurations—such as radial or axial exhaust—and options like bleeds, controlled extractions to match specific process requirements.

faqs.q: What is the typical steam pressure and temperature range for industrial steam turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy industrial steam turbines are designed for steam inlet pressures of 103 to 160 bar(a) and temperatures from 400 to 565 °C, with some models accommodating even wider ranges.

As a market leader for industrial steam turbines, Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive range of reliable and versatile steam turbines for the power output range from 2 to 250 MW. The industrial steam turbines are designed for easy constructability, fast start-up and economical operation. The inlet steam pressure is 103 to 160 bar(a) and the inlet steam temperature is 400 to 565 °C.

Power generation for world’s largest single-phase pulp mill project

The Sucuriú Project, recognized as the world's largest single-phase project of its kind, will establish a new pulp mill with an impressive capacity of 3.5 million tons per year of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp. Siemens Energy is set to power this project with steam turbines, generators and a distribution system. The project will feature the largest Siemens Energy steam turbine generator units in single casing ever supplied to the Pulp Mill industry.

The plant will be operated sustainably on the basis of biomass and will feed 220 MW of electrical energy into the grid with an installed capacity of 636 MW thanks to efficient combined heat and power generation.

The sheer weight is impressive: more than 500 tons! A steam turbine, gearbox, generator, condenser, and auxiliary systems are all packed onto one base frame. The “Single Lift” concept can easily be installed once on-site. Customers´ demand for flexible installation requirements—small footprint, short installation and commissioning time at the site, high availability, and enhanced string test possibilities—has driven the development of these packages. Watch the video and learn more

The SST-800 is a single casing steam turbine with center steam admission and reverse steam flow inner casing, designed for a direct coupled generator or mechanical drive.

The highly customized turbine provides for an outstanding efficiency, fast start-up times and high reliability and availability. It supports all requirements for economical installation and operation in combination with highest flexibility for complex industrial processes. A double or even multicasing solution can also be provided.

The SST-800 steam turbine can be used for both condensing and back-pressure applications. Turbine auxiliary systems are also designed as pre-engineered modules covering the complete range of turbine sizes.

The turbine can be arranged on a foundation or as a package (includung oil system and on a base frame). The SST-800 steam turbine design is in accordance with DIN or API standards.

The SST-700 / 900 is a standard turbine solution with short delivery time due to its fixed pre-engineered design. Predefined modules enable a short manufacturing period, cost-efficient material supply and a fast ex-works delivery.

The straight flow turbine solution with power output of up to 250 MW consists of a geared high-pressure steam turbine (backpressure), an intermediate / low-pressure steam turbine (condensing), both driving a generator installed in between.

The dual casing reheat turbine configuration with inner casing is a competitive and optimized product for combined cycle power plants and concentrated solar power plants.

We deliver a standard steam turbine generator set including the SST-600 (with or without gearbox), a generator, oil system, piping and instrumentation and the control system. The standard package can be extended to include a condenser, condensing plant or pre-heating system. The SST-600 with its reliable and flexible design is available with axial or radial exhaust.

The SST-600 is also an efficient and economic mechanical drive. Since the 1970s, hundreds of projects have been successfully implemented all over the world using the SST-600 to directly drive everything from the smallest boiler feedwater pump just as reliably as the largest compressor even in the most complex processes. The SST-600 complies with regulations including the API standard.

The SST-500 is a single casing, double exhaust flow steam turbine, which can be used as an entire drive or as the lowpressure module of a multiple-casing turboset, directly driven or geared. This turbine, with its capacity to operate over a wide range of speed and power, is ideal for large steam volume flows. Steam flows into the turbine via two tangential inlets to equalize thermal loading and blade stress.

Emergency stop valves and control valves are installed in the steam inlet pipes. The steam flows tangentially into the inner casing and then axially to both exhausts. The customized design of the steam path allows exact adjustment to surpass general physical limitations of the last stage blades. Double-end drive is available, if required, e.g. for booster pump drive

The SST-400 is a single casing steam turbine, providing geared or direct drive to 50 and 60 Hz generators, or to compressors and pumps. The symmetrical casing with horizontal joint flange enables the SST-400 to accept short start-up times and rapid load changes.

items.body:
Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive range of steam turbine products in the power output range from 90 to 1,900 MW. Do you have a question regarding our products, solutions and services?

The compact arrangement features a two-cylinder design with an axial exhaust for use in combined cycle power plants.

The SST-3000 series covers the power output range from 90 to 275 MW. It features a separate high-pressure (HP) turbine and combined intermediate-pressure / low-pressure (IP / LP) turbine with single flow axial exhaust for 50 and 60 Hz applications.

The SST-4000 series is our specialized turbine for non-reheat, combined cycle applications. With the specialized design of the blade path, the entire power range from 100 to 500 MW can be covered with the highest reliability and availability. More than 40 turbines of this type are already in operation or in the commissioning stage, with a total installed capacity of approximately 8,200 MW.

The SST-4000 series consists of an intermediate-pressure and a low-pressure turbine. The installation is either high or low level arrangement with down, double-side or single-side exhaust. The turbine is able to provide process steam e. g. for industries or sea water desalination and can provide industrial heating.

Thanks to its systematically modular design, the SST-4000 series can easily be adapted to the individual operating conditions and thermal cycle design of the plant. Its fast installation, thanks to prefabricated, tested modules delivered ready for connection, is of additional advantage.

Siemens Energy Steam Turbines of the SST-5000 series are operated in combined cycle power plants (CCPP) and in steam power plants (SPP).

The SST-5000 steam turbine combined with a gas turbine, is able to achieve a net plant efficiency of more than 64 percent in combined cycle applications.

Siemens Energy Steam Turbines of the SST-6000 series are widely operated in steam power plants with a power output up to 1,200 MW and an efficiency up to more than 46 percent.

Products of the SST-6000 series consist of a high-pressure turbine, an intermediate-pressure (IP) turbine, and up to three low-pressure turbines for 50 and 60 Hz.

The SST-6000 is installed as a high-level arrangement with down exhaust. Various extractions (up to 10 stages) are possible for feed water preheating, process steam, and district heating. The installed capacity of SST-6000 all over the world is more than 100,000 MW.

Siemens Energy Steam Turbines of the SST-9000 series are highly reliable for the application in conventional islands of advanced pressurized water reactors in nuclear power plants, with a power output up to 1,900 MW.

The half-speed (25 turns per second) SST-9000 series consists of a double-flow high-pressure saturated steam turbine (HD) and up to three twin-flow low-pressure turbines (ND) with shrunk-on wheel disc rotors. Siemens low-pressure turbines with shrunk-on wheel discs represent technology that has been proven over decades. The result: no stress corrosion cracking and thus no replacement of the low-pressure rotor or wheel discs during the excepted service life.

faqs.q: California Independent System Operator (CAISO)
faqs.a: As grid connection experts, Siemens Energy can provide support to ensure IEEE P2800.2 conformance through validated dynamic/EMT model for the interconnection and plant level commissioning tests. Qstor™ enables participation in CAISO’s energy and ancillary services markets, including:

faqs.q: Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT)
faqs.a: Siemens Energy also supports full IEEE P2800.2 compliance for ERCOT, with validated models and commissioning support tailored to Texas grid requirements. Qstor™ enables participation in ERCOT’s energy and ancillary services markets, including:

faqs.q: What is a battery energy storage system?
faqs.a: A Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is a technology-based solution that stores electrical energy using rechargeable batteries for later use. These systems are used in various applications, including stabilizing the electrical grid, supporting renewable energy sources like solar or wind, and providing backup power during outages.

faqs.q: How does a battery energy storage system work?
faqs.a: A BESS stores energy by converting electricity into chemical energy within batteries. When energy is needed, the system converts the stored chemical energy back into usable electricity. Components such as batteries, inverters, and a battery management system work together to ensure efficient energy storage and delivery.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of BESS?
faqs.a: Supports renewable energy: BESS help manage the variability of solar and wind energy. Grid stability: Balancing energy supply and demand. Cost savings: reduction of electricity costs by shifting energy use to off-peak times. Backup power: BESS provide reliable power during outages. Environmental benefits: BESS reduce reliance on fossil fuels when paired with renewables.

faqs.q: What is the largest BESS project in the world?
faqs.a: The largest Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in the world is the Edwards & Sanborn solar-plus-storage project in California. It has a storage capacity of 3,287MWh and is paired with 875MWdc of solar PV. Located on 4,600 acres in Kern County, the project uses battery units from LG Chem, Samsung, and BYD. It surpasses the previous largest BESS at Moss Landing, also in California, and is designed to enhance grid resilience while supporting renewable energy integration.

faqs.q: How to store energy in a battery?
faqs.a: Energy is stored in a battery during the charging process. Electricity is converted into chemical energy, which is held within the battery until it is needed. When discharged, this chemical energy is converted back into electrical energy for use.

faqs.q: What is the cost of battery energy storage systems?
faqs.a: The cost of a BESS depends on factors such as size, battery type, and application. Larger systems and advanced battery technologies tend to cost more, but prices are declining as the industry grows and technology improves.

faqs.q: How long can energy be stored in a battery? What is the typical lifespan of a BESS?
faqs.a: Energy storage duration: Batteries typically store energy for a few hours, though some technologies are designed for longer durations. Lifespan: The typical lifespan of a BESS depends on the battery type, maintenance, and usage patterns, but it generally lasts several years.

faqs.q: How do BESS support the electrical grid?
faqs.a: Frequency regulation: Keeps the grid stable by quickly responding to fluctuations in supply and demand. Energy shifting: Stores excess energy during low-demand times and releases it during high-demand periods. Renewable energy support: Helps integrate solar and wind energy by smoothing out their variability. Black start capability: Restores power to the grid after a blackout.

faqs.q: What are the critical components of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and their functions?
faqs.a: Batteries: The core component where energy is stored in chemical form and converted back into electricity when needed. Common battery types include lithium-ion, lead-acid, and flow batteries. Battery management system (BMS): Ensures safe and efficient operation by monitoring and controlling factors such as temperature, voltage, and state of charge. Power conversion system (PCS): Includes inverters and converters to transform direct current (DC) stored in batteries into alternating current (AC) for grid use, and vice versa during charging. Energy management system (EMS): Manages the overall operation of the BESS, including energy dispatch, grid interaction, and optimization of performance. Thermal management system: Regulates the temperature of the batteries to prevent overheating and ensure optimal performance and safety. Protection and safety systems: Includes fire suppression, fault detection, and isolation mechanisms to prevent hazards like thermal runaway or electrical faults. Communication and control systems: Enable remote monitoring, diagnostics, and integration with the power grid or renewable energy sources.

faqs.q: How do BESS integrate with renewable energy sources and the power grid?
faqs.a: Renewable energy integration: BESS store excess energy generated by intermittent renewable sources like solar and wind during periods of low demand. This stored energy can be discharged when renewable generation is low or demand is high, ensuring a consistent energy supply. Grid connection: BESS are connected to the power grid to provide services such as energy dispatch, frequency regulation, and load balancing. They can absorb surplus energy from the grid or release stored energy to meet demand. Peak shaving: BESS help reduce the strain on the grid by supplying energy during peak demand periods, minimizing the need for fossil-fuel-based peaker plants. Microgrid and off-grid applications: BESS can operate in conjunction with renewable energy sources in microgrids or off-grid systems, providing reliable power in remote areas.

items.body:

items.title: Compressed Air Energy Storage
items.description: Compressed air energy storage is a longterm storage solution basing on thermal mechanical principle.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of CAES compared to other energy storage technologies?
faqs.a: Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) offers several advantages over other energy storage technologies, making it a compelling choice for large-scale energy management. It relies on well-proven components such as expanders, compressors, and gas turbines, which are widely used in various industrial applications, enhancing reliability and reducing risks associated with new technologies. The use of air as a storage medium is a significant strength, as it is readily available and easy to obtain, eliminating concerns related to resource scarcity. CAES systems can store energy for much longer periods compared to battery storage systems, making them particularly suitable for applications requiring extended energy supply. Additionally, CAES can respond quickly when unloading, typically in less than ten minutes, and can absorb excess electricity within five minutes, providing a flexible solution for energy management and enhancing grid stability.

faqs.q: What are the challenges or disadvantages of CAES?
faqs.a: While Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) offers several advantages, it also faces some challenges One significant challenge is the requirement for suitable geological formations to store compressed air, as underground caverns or reservoirs are necessary for effective operation. This can limit the locations where CAES can be implemented. Furthermore, the initial capital investment for setting up a CAES facility can be substantial, requiring significant financial resources and long-term planning.

faqs.q: Where can compressed air energy storage (CAES) facilities be built?
faqs.a: Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) facilities can be built in locations that have suitable geological formations for storing compressed air. Ideal sites typically include underground caverns, such as salt domes, depleted natural gas fields, or aquifers, which can effectively contain the high-pressure air. These geological formations provide the necessary structural integrity to withstand the pressures involved in the storage process. Additionally, CAES facilities should be located near renewable energy sources, such as wind or solar farms, to take advantage of excess energy generation during peak production times. Proximity to existing electrical infrastructure is also important to facilitate the integration of the stored energy into the power grid. While the availability of suitable geological sites can limit the locations for CAES facilities, the latest developments are examining pipelines and subsea locations as alternative options for compressed air storage. This innovation may expand the range of viable locations for CAES systems, allowing for greater flexibility in site selection and implementation.

faqs.q: How is thermal energy managed in compressed air energy storage (CAES)?
faqs.a: In Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES), the clever management of thermal energy is the wit behind the solution, as it plays a crucial role in the system’s efficiency and overall performance. During the compression process, air is compressed and heated due to the increase in pressure. This heat can be managed in one of two ways: Adiabatic Compression: In adiabatic CAES systems, the heat generated during compression is captured and stored, allowing for a clever reuse of thermal energy during the expansion phase. When the compressed air is released to generate electricity, this stored heat enhances efficiency, showcasing the brilliance of thermal energy management. Diabatic Compression: In traditional diabatic CAES systems, the heat generated during compression is not captured, and the compressed air is cooled before storage. While this approach simplifies system design, it can lead to energy losses, emphasizing the importance of effective thermal management. When the stored compressed air is released to drive a turbine, the thermal energy management system ensures that the air is at the optimal temperature for efficient expansion. If the air is too cold, it can hinder performance, making it clear that the success of CAES relies heavily on the artful management of thermal energy. Thus, the wit of CAES lies in its ability to harness and optimize thermal energy, maximizing energy output and ensuring reliable operation.

faqs.q: Can CAES integrate with renewable energy sources?
faqs.a: Yes, Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) can effectively integrate with renewable energy sources, which was part of the initial idea behind its development. By utilizing excess energy generated from renewable sources such as wind and solar, CAES systems can store this energy in the form of compressed air during periods of high production. This stored energy can then be released to generate electricity when demand is high or when renewable generation is low, providing a reliable and flexible energy solution. In addition to renewable energy integration, CAES systems are also suitable for use in industrial parks, chemical plants, and other facilities with significant energy demands. These environments can benefit from the ability to store excess energy and manage fluctuations in power supply, enhancing operational efficiency and reducing reliance on traditional energy sources.

faqs.q: What are the different types of CAES technologies offered by Siemens Energy?
faqs.a: Adiabatic Compression: In adiabatic CAES systems, the heat generated during compression is captured and stored, allowing for a clever reuse of thermal energy during the expansion phase. The adiabatic CAES cycle stores energy in form of pressure in a cavern, while compression heat is stored in a thermal storage. For re-electrification both forms of energy are being utilized. No additional fuel is needed to heat up the released air. . Diabatic Compression: In traditional diabatic CAES systems, the compressed air is cooled before storage. Diabatic storage units dissipate part of the compression heat into the atmosphere with intercoolers. The air must be reheated to be returned to the CAES cycle. Energy and ancillary services with low fuel consumption provide best efficiency.

items.body:
Thermal mechanical long-term storage is an innovative energy storage technology that utilizes thermodynamics to store electrical energy as thermal energy for extended periods.

Siemens Energy Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) is a comprehensive, proven, grid-scale energy storage solution. We support projects from conceptual design through commercial operation and beyond. Our CAES solution includes all the associated above ground systems, plant engineering, procurement, construction, installation, start-up services and long term service support.

Discover longtime storage - thermal mechanical storage solutions!

As renewable power generation from wind and solar grows in its contribution to the world’s energy mix, utilities will need to balance the generation variability of these sustainable resources with demandfluctuations. Power-generation operators can use compressed air energy storage (CAES) technology for a reliable, cost-effective, and long-duration energy storage solution at grid scale.

Siemens Energy CAES improves utilization of renewable energy resources by absorbing GW-hours of energy that would otherwise be curtailed and provides grid balancing and reserve services with lower fuel usage and carbon footprint than other controllable resources.

Revitalization of Pioneering Compressed Air Storage Technology

Siemens Energy and PowerSouth Energy Cooperative (PowerSouth) will revitalize the pioneering Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) power plant in McIntosh, Alabama, a technology that has been at the forefront of energy efficiency since the early 1990s. This technology allows for the storage of excess electricity during periods of high generation, which can then be fed back into the grid when demand peaks, thus providing a reliable and stable energy supply.

This marks a significant step towards enhancing the reliability of sustainable energy. The CAES technology, which is utilized in only a handful of plants worldwide, will undergo revitalization through repairs and upgrades to improve reliability.

Siemens Energy will re-engineer and service the expander, ensuring that this power plant can continue to operate efficiently for decades to come. The agreement underscores the commitment of both Siemens Energy and PowerSouth to harness innovative solutions for the energy challenges of the future. As we look towards an energy system with an increasing presence of renewables, the role of CAES becomes increasingly valuable. It offers a grid-stabilizing function that is conducive to integrating renewable energy into the existing infrastructure. Siemens Energy is committed to developing complete solution packages that encompass everything from plant planning and installation to ongoing service and support.

For CAES technology to be rolled out on a larger scale, collaboration among stakeholders, investment in infrastructure, and continued innovation are essential. Siemens Energy is dedicated to leading the charge in this area, ensuring that we can meet the energy demands of the future while prioritizing sustainability and efficiency.

This project is not just a milestone for Siemens Energy and PowerSouth; it is a testament to our shared vision for a more efficient and reliable energy future. Together, we are taking a significant step toward the future, revitalizing a technology that will play a crucial role in the energy landscape for years to come.

Diabatic storage units dissipate part of the compression heat into the atmosphere with intercoolers. The air must be reheated to be returned to the CAES cycle. Energy and ancillary services with low fuel consumption provide best efficiency.

items.description: Marine electric propulsion/drives solutions from Siemens combine excellent performance, uncompromising reliability, and maximum efficiency.

faqs.q: Electrical power system
faqs.a: BlueDrive PlusC – electrical power system The synchronous generators are designed to operate in the same speed and power range as the connected diesel engine. Due to extended development of the power electronics, the main drive unit BlueDrive PlusC is created as a stand-alone, integrated unit, including the generator and bus-tie panel as well as the frequency converter controls for all thrusters and auxiliary drives. In addition, the unit provides clean power supply to all auxiliary consumers, and all electronics are based on known and well-proven technology. In addition to the operational advantages, the new unit reduces footprint, volume, and weight by at least 30 percent.

faqs.q: Power station control system
faqs.a: BlueDrive PlusC – power station control system The BlueDrive PlusC unit is equipped with an integrated control system that realizes all genset control, drive control and power management functions within the unit itself. The speed and power of the diesel engines is controlled in correspondence with the total power consumption of the vessel. The electric system is only fed with active power from the generators; hence there is no circulating reactive power to handle. The speed and power characteristics of the diesel engine will be parameterized according to the selected diesel engine type. Integrated parts of the system are Power Management (PMS), Power Plant Protection (P3) and Generator Power Adaption Systems (GPA). All these systems are integrated in the integrated control system of the BlueDrive PlusC.

faqs.q: BlueDrive Eco
faqs.a: The BlueDrive PlusC for small vessels: BlueDrive Eco BlueDrive Eco combines the experience from both systems BlueDrive PlusC and EcoProp. EcoProp is well known as a flexible, compact, high-power diesel-electric propulsion system for smaller vessels such as yachts, ferries, and public authority vessels. Like the complete BlueDrive family, BlueDrive Eco uses the Siemens Energy industrial converter platform components, providing very high reliability and availability. It enables scalable systems from 5 kW inverter power use and closes the power range (to BlueDrive PlusC up to 5.5 MW inverter power), all in the same topology.

faqs.q: BlueVault™
faqs.a: The Siemens Energy Storage System (ESS): BlueVault The advanced lithium-ion battery-based solution BlueVault for offshore installations and marine vessels is suited for both all-electric and hybrid energy-storage applications. BlueVault energy storage solutions are designed to help ensure continuity of power and to minimize carbon dioxide emissions. The battery is designed to maximize life, performance, and safety. It is equipped with an integrated battery management system and overload/short circuit protection. The storage modules with 6.6 kWh Li-Ion batteries can be slid into a rack. The battery storage cubicle consists of 9 modules and 60 kWh. The cubicles can be easily lined up to the total required battery capacity.

faqs.q: What are Siemens Energy’s electric propulsion solutions for marine vessels?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive portfolio of electric and diesel-electric propulsion systems, shaft generators, podded drives, and energy storage solutions designed to improve efficiency, reliability, and environmental performance across commercial and naval vessels.

faqs.q: How do marine electric propulsion systems improve vessel efficiency?
faqs.a: Electric propulsion allows engines to operate closer to their optimal load point, reducing specific fuel consumption and emissions while enabling flexible power distribution to thrusters and auxiliary systems.

faqs.q: What is diesel-electric propulsion and how does it work?
faqs.a: In diesel-electric propulsion, diesel generators produce electrical power that feeds frequency converters and electric motors, which in turn drive the propellers, decoupling engine speed from propeller speed and enabling highly efficient, flexible operation.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of diesel-electric marine propulsion?
faqs.a: Key benefits include reduced fuel consumption, therefore lower emissions, quieter and low-vibration operation, and higher operational flexibility.

faqs.q: How does SISHIP BlueDrive Eco support hybrid and fully electric vessels?
faqs.a: SISHIP BlueDrive Eco supports hybrid and fully electric vessels by using a compact, DC based power system that can combine diesel generators, batteries, and alternative energy sources into one flexible propulsion architecture. Its modular design allows vessels to operate efficiently in diesel electric, hybrid, or zero emission modes while maintaining stable power distribution and high overall system efficiency.

faqs.q: What advantages does SISHIP BlueDrive PlusC offer for marine propulsion?
faqs.a: Through its redundant topology SISHIP BlueDrive PlusC is a highly reliable propulsion system that enables individual speed control of engines, optimizes operational profiles for minimal fuel consumption, supports dynamic positioning, easily integrates other energy sources such as fuel cell and batteries, and offers a sophisticated power management system in one compact system.

faqs.q: How does the BlueVault energy storage system enhance marine propulsion?
faqs.a: BlueVault lithium-ion battery systems support all-electric and hybrid power plants by providing energy storage for peak shaving, spinning reserve, and backup power, significantly reducing onboard fuel consumption, emissions, and engine running hours.

faqs.q: What is the SGM shaft generator with motor function and why is it important?
faqs.a: The Shaft Generator with Motor function is a PTO/PTI system (power take-off/power take-in) that can work both as a shaft generator (PTO) and as a shaft motor (PTI) enabling electrical power generation and propulsion boost while reducing fuel consumption and emissions and supporting integration with waste-heat recovery or hybrid concepts.

items.body:
The propulsion system has the biggest influence on performance, security, and cost-effectiveness. Fuel consumption, as the greatest single cost item, holds the biggest cost-saving potential for a ship’s operation.

Moreover, the choice of a suitable propulsion system influences a whole host of other factors:

Siemens Energy's integrated drive system concepts help you find the right technology for your purposes.

Siemens Energy offers future-proof electric propulsion/drives solutions for the safe, efficient, and reliable operation of commercial as well as naval vessels.

Our two diesel-electric marine propulsion systems reduce fuel requirements, increase maneuverability, minimize environmental risks, and make your ship quieter and more comfortable.

Designed without compromising power output and fail-safe performance, our Drive MV integrated drive system offers an almost unlimited power range.

In the Permasyn motor for submarines, excitation is achieved with permanent magnets. This results in outstanding features in terms of uncompromising reliability and operational readiness.

Siemens Energy developed the SGM shaft generator with motor function in response to rising fuel costs and ever-stricter environmental regulations.

With BlueDrive Eco, the BlueDrive family is now offering scalable solutions for all drive requirements, covering diverse performance graduations for small to medium-sized drives, from 5 KW in auxiliary mode up to 5.5 MW in main drives.

With their outstanding reliability, minimized noise signature, and stray field development, Siemens Energy DC-Prop DC drives are perfectly suitable for operation in submarines.

Diesel-electric propulsion systems are gaining more and more importance in shipping. Shipping installations with higher fuel efficiency in all operational stages will be increasingly favored and will presumably have great potential for future growth. Drive LV is the leading technology solution.

Diesel-electric marine propulsion systems reduce fuel requirements, increase maneuverability, minimize environmental risks, and make your ship quieter and more comfortable. However, their main advantage lies in the exceptional degree of fail-safety that Drive LV attains, thanks to its redundant system design. Indeed, Drive LV is the most reliable diesel-electric propulsion system ever built, making it a future-proof solution which helps to ensure the competitiveness of your vessels for the long term.

Profit from a perfectly planned system consisting of diesel generators, low-voltage switchgear, frequency converter, and drive motors in combination with an ingenious propulsion control and monitoring system.

Diesel-electric propulsion systems are clearly superior both technically and in operation to normal diesel drive systems in almost all areas. Drive MV is the marine industry’s leading alternating-current propulsion system. Although it can unleash much power, it runs as quiet as a whisper with low vibration.

Designed without compromising power output and fail-safe performance, our Drive MV integrated drive system offers an almost unlimited power range. In addition to its high energy efficiency and low environmental impact, it is also marked by its quiet, low-vibration operation. And thanks to its state-of-the-art propulsion-control components and software, Drive MV allows vessels to be maneuvered with the highest precision.

Its redundancy design ensures the highest possible level of reliability. Right from the design phase, its simple, compact, and modular construction using standardized components provides maximum flexibility and scope and allows for worldwide availability of spare parts and ease of maintenance.

Submarines are the vessels that depend most on the complete reliability and operational readiness of their propulsion motors. A drive system that operates efficiently with very low signatures is essential for long dives and makes the boat harder to detect. The Permasyn motor for submarines is smaller and more lightweight than conventional propulsion solutions – and it achieves much better efficiency at extremely low signatures.

In the Permasyn motor for submarines, excitation is achieved with permanent magnets. This results in outstanding features in terms of uncompromising reliability and operational readiness, combined with high efficiency and extremely low signature values. The replacement of the electrical exciter by a permanent magnet makes possible extremely small and lightweight motors with high power density and high torque over the entire speed range. This enables the use of a larger propeller with significantly higher efficiency.
